Smaller numbers supported the Forest of Ulnak spy network, the three Wintermark beacons, and Bounders, Drakes, Fire of the South, Golden Axe, Gryphon's Pride, Lions of Adelmar, Red Wind Corsairs, Sparrows Reckoning, Star Forged, Strong Reeds and Tusks.

n.Dawn: Many Dawnish nobles from Astolat, Semmerholm, the Barrens and Weirwater were honoured, chiefly for the Citadel Guard and Eastern Sky, alongside Burning Falcon, Gryphon's Pride, Lions of Adelmar, Golden Axe, Drakes and the Forest of Ulnak spy network.
n.Highguard: Highborn from Bastion, Casinea, Necropolis and Reikos were honoured for the Citadel Guard and Eastern Sky, including the Cohort of the Winter Bear and the Steel Tide, with a few from Reikos supporting Burning Falcon.
n.Imperial Orcs: Orcs from Mareave and Skarsind, among them Pathfinders, Sand Vipers, Stonesworn and Bloodcrows, were honoured for supporting Eastern Sky.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: a handful of Navarr from Therunin, Miaren, Hercynia and the Barrens are listed supporting Burning Falcon, the Citadel Guard and Golden Axe.
n.The Brass Coast: Citizens from Feroz, Kahraman, Segura and Madruga were honoured for Burning Falcon, Red Wind Corsairs, Star Forged, Fire of the South, Drakes and Eastern Sky.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: a few League citizens from Tassato, Sarvos and Temeschwar are listed supporting the Citadel Guard, Eastern Sky and Sparrows Reckoning.
n.The Marches: Marchers from Bregasland, Upwold, Mitwold and Mournwold were honoured, notably for Burning Falcon, alongside the Tusks, Strong Reeds, Bounders, Drakes, Eastern Sky and the Citadel Guard.
n.Urizen: Urizeni from Morrow, Redoubt, Zenith, Sarangrave and Spiral were honoured in numbers for the Citadel Guard and Eastern Sky, with Tropaion and Urizen, Whole prominent among the banners.
n.Varushka: Varushkans from Karov, Karsk, Miekarova, Ossium and Volodmartz were honoured for the Citadel Guard and Eastern Sky, with two from Ossium backing the Tsirku spy network and one Burning Falcon.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark dominated support for the Tsirku spy network and the Beacons of Hahnmark, Kallavesa and Sermersuaq, and many of its citizens were also honoured for Burning Falcon, Eastern Sky, Fire of the South and the Citadel Guard.

t.Tsirku: More than two dozen citizens, overwhelmingly from Wintermark's Hahnmark, Kallavesa and Sermersuaq with two from Varushka's Ossium, were honoured for supporting a spy network in Tsirku.

Asavean Factor.d: The Loyalty Assembly, which values the Asavean project above the grand construction in Bastion, could raise one of two competing year-long mandates. One would arrange a face-to-face meeting between a named individual and one of the six identified Asavean factions. The other would press the heralds of a named eternal for aid. Whichever wins forecloses the other path. The Senate might also commission an appraisal into how Loyal citizens could support the project, though its backing is uncertain and the choice of prognosticator would matter greatly. Through his herald Zand, Callidus offered white granite in exchange for items of profound significance, such as pilgrim shields, true liao, the liberty pact pen or even the Imperial Crown, negotiated through the Archmage of Autumn's plenipotentiary.

n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the Asaveans' support for the Grendel in their war on the Empire is cited as a reason the Senate may be cool towards the project.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: the grand construction in Bastion is referred to only as the project the Loyalty Assembly values less than anchoring the Way in Asavea.

t.Bastion: Mentioned in passing: Bastion is named as the site of the Empire's other grand construction, which the Loyalty Assembly ranks below its Asavean effort.

Beneath a moonless sky.d: The festival celebrates the victory over the Cult of the Falconer and years of good relations fostered by Raal Dunn, Mediator of Hyljehal. Koskinen warned that the orcs of Fjorknae, paid with Meade's plundered gold, had sent a warband to aid the Lasambrians, raising the risk of piracy. Rebuilding a smuggler's cove in Tromsa would open the voyage Sail into the Cold, and later Raid into the Cold. He asked for a Wintermark story performance, offering hylje tales of Sermersuaq and the Rusalka in return. Given three measures of stardust, the hylje could aid exploration of Tsirku, with more help possible if the Empire took Skyfall Waste and the Icewood.

n.Jotun: The orcs of Fjorknae give fealty to a Jarl of Jarls, though nobody knows which. The hylje would offer their fullest help with Tsirku only if the Empire seized Skyfall Waste in Tromsa from the Jotun.
n.Wintermark: Up to fifty Wintermarkers were invited to an unprecedented hylje festival, with the Mediator of Hyljehal asked to arrange a story performance and to bring stardust. Wintermark fleets were also offered a scouting voyage against Fjorknae.

t.Fjorknae: Its little-known orcs had been paid by the Lasambrians to send a large warband, might stay or even send a navy, and were once close to the violent akhlut. A Wintermark voyage could reveal who they are and whom they serve, then turn to raiding their settlements.
t.Hahnmark: Mentioned in passing: Koskinen believed some smiths of Hahnmark know how to make the stardust the hylje need.
t.Kallavesa: Mentioned in passing: the Kallavesa are named as good friends of the hylje and expressly included in the festival invitation.
t.Sea of Snow: Koskinen warned of a heightened risk of piracy for those sailing the Sea of Snow, given the activity of the Fjorknae orcs.
t.Sermersuaq: Home of the Hyljehal and the Suaq, the hylje's close kin, Sermersuaq was to be enchanted by a hylje ritual of Autumn magic during the festival. The hylje would also tell their tale of the legendary Sermersuaq herself.
t.Tromsa: Re-establishing a smuggler's cove in Tromsa would restore intelligence gathering there and open the Sail into the Cold voyage. Taking Skyfall Waste and the Icewood from the Jotun would greatly increase hylje help in Tsirku.
t.Tsirku: With three measures of stardust to protect them from the Northern Lights, the hylje offered to aid exploration of the region containing Nutjuitoq, cutting the scouting needed by a fifth. With Skyfall Waste in Imperial hands, they could also aid with Karnakadatha's region, cutting it by two fifths for both.

r.Sermersuaq/Suaq Fount: Holding the Fount alongside the Suaq Wastes, Skyfall Waste and the Icewood would give the Empire control of access to Tsirku's southern lakes. Hylje-aided scouts would cross Nutjuitoq rather than head north-west from the Fount.
r.Sermersuaq/Suaq Wastes: The hylje would aid scouts crossing Nutjuitoq into Tsirku from the Suaq Wastes. Keeping the Wastes is part of controlling access to Tsirku's southern lakes.
r.Tromsa/Icewood: If the Empire held the Icewood along with Skyfall Waste and the Suaq lands, it would control access to Tsirku's southern lakes, letting the hylje move freely between them.
r.Tromsa/Skyfall Waste: Seizing Skyfall Waste from the Jotun would let the hylje also aid exploration of Karnakadatha's region and raise their help to two fifths for both regions.

Chains from the deep.d: A Synod mandate sending a named individual with true liao this season would create an aura of Vigilance over the Great Chain, permanently doubling the benefit of wains spent on emergency resupply, repairing the bastion or replenishing the garrison. If consecrated, the League could within a year build the Cathedral of Links in Cigno, creating a Bishop of the Links with 18 liao a season; Sarvosi would match wains spent on its grandeur. A fortification commission could also let fleets guard the Chain. Skathe offered, if the League National Assembly declared her a worthy player of the Great Game and 500 tempest jade and 500 beggar's lye were provided, to curse the Chain to inflict extra casualties on attackers.

n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel are named as the likely besiegers of Sarvos while Imperial armies are stretched east and west.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: competitive Sarvosi do not want to be outdone by the Highborn next door in defending the Bay, and Skathe recalls a troublesome Highguard coven.
n.The League: The League was offered a chance to sanctify Sarvos's Great Chain, build a grand cathedral to restore the city's prestige against Holberg, strengthen its harbour defences, and decide whether to court Skathe, whose earlier attack on Sarvos many still resent.

t.Bastion: Mentioned in passing: Capodomus Cathedral in Sarvos is called the most stunning cathedral outside Bastion.
t.Bay of Catazar: Expanding the Chain would let Imperial fleets help guard Sarvos the next time pirates from the Bay of Catazar attack the city.
t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: Holberg is the current greatest city in the League, and Sarvosi hope a new cathedral could give them an edge in a future rematch.
t.Sarvos: Sarvos could gain a consecrated Great Chain that strengthens resupply of its defences, a new cathedral funded partly by its own merchant princes, fleet-guarded fortifications, and possibly a curse from Skathe on its defences.

r.Sarvos/Cigno: Both the proposed Cathedral of Links on the main dock and the commission to expand the Great Chain would be built in Cigno, provided the Chain is first consecrated.

Construct Archives of the Advisor.d: Proposed by Merari Navigators of Virtue, Senator for the Bastion, and seconded by Pathfinder Gaddak, Senator for Mareave, the motion commissioned a sinecure in Solvihill and amended the title of Advisor on Orc Affairs to hold it. The construction required standard costs, 10 wains of white granite and 30 crowns in labour, and took three months. After the Summer Solstice Frith provided 3 thrones 6 crowns and the 10 wains of white granite. With the Archives complete, the Advisor on Orc Affairs receives 12 measures of iridescent gloaming each season, starting at the Winter Solstice 388YE.

n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orcs' homeland of Skarsind gained a new sinecure, and the Advisor on Orc Affairs, the title tied to their affairs, now draws 12 measures of iridescent gloaming each season.

t.Skarsind: Skarsind, held by the Imperial Orcs, became home to the Archives of the Advisor, a newly completed sinecure.

r.Skarsind/Solvihill: The Archives of the Advisor were built in Solvihill using white granite and labour paid for by Frith, and were completed in time to yield gloaming from the Winter Solstice 388YE.

Construct Bears Rest.d: The commission required ten wains of mithril and 30 crowns of labour on top of the standard costs, and would take three months to build. After the Summer Solstice 388YE, Bjorn provided the ten wains of mithril and 3 thrones 5 crowns, and Rhys Nighthaven gave a further crown. Once complete, the title of Steward of Bears Rest is to be appointed by unanimous decision of the Wintermark senators. The steward is responsible for collecting the mana carried down the river from the melting glacier upstream.

n.Wintermark: Wintermark gains a new mana sinecure in its own lands, and its senators must agree unanimously on who holds the title of Steward of Bears Rest.

t.Hahnmark: Hahnmark is the site of the Bears Rest commission, a sinecure gathering mana from a glacier-fed river in the territory.

r.Hahnmark/Northspires: Bears Rest was to be built in Northspires, where its steward would collect mana flowing down the river from the melting glacier upstream.

Construct Clattering Curtain Theatre.d: Proposed by Cesare Sanguineo Rezia Di Tassato, Senator for Tassato, and seconded by Vasilmir Radovanovna Esskivic, Senator for Miekarova, the motion authorised a theatre in Tassato Mestra. It created the tenured title of Martim de Tassato's Clattering Curtain Theatre Champion, to be appointed by unanimous vote of the League's senators. Construction required 12 wains of white granite and 36 crowns in labour on top of standard costs, and would take three months. After the Summer Solstice, Esme Beatrix de Holberg provided 4 thrones 4 crowns and the 12 wains of white granite. Once complete, the League senators may appoint the Champion.

n.The League: The League gains a new tenured, money-producing sinecure whose Champion its senators must appoint by unanimous vote once the theatre is complete.

t.Tassato: Tassato's senator proposed the theatre, which honours Martim de Tassato and will stand in the territory's capital region.

r.Tassato/Tassato Mestra: Mestra is to host the new Clattering Curtain Theatre, built from white granite over three months with materials and funds supplied by Esme Beatrix de Holberg.

Construct Nightingale Chorus.d: The wayhouse was announced under an Imperial Wayleave. It required 25 wains of white granite, 10 wains of weirwood, 105 crowns in labour and three months to build. Many contributors provided materials and money after the Summer Solstice and Autumn Equinox of 388YE, including Corwyn Heartsbane, Lady Mercy Goldvein and Morgoth SweetBlood. Once complete, it would increase investment in Astolat for military units engaged in the Quest Against the Vallorn, add one throne per season to Astolat's taxation, and let Navarr take a free personal resource in Astolat. It would also create the title of Conductor of the Nightingale Chorus, elected by Cat's Graces. Weirwater and Semmerholm would benefit too if the Dawnish Assembly named the fight against the Vallorn their highest calling.

n.Dawn: Dawnish-held Astolat would gain a throne of tax each season and stronger support for armies fighting the Vallorn. The Dawnish Assembly could extend that support to Weirwater and Semmerholm by naming the fight against the Vallorn their highest calling.
n.Navarr: The wayhouse was announced by Mharen Splitroot, Bearer of an Imperial Wayleave. Once complete, Navarr could take a new personal resource in Astolat for free in the season of its completion.

t.Astolat: Astolat would host the wayhouse and gain one throne of taxation per season. Military units engaged in the Quest Against the Vallorn there would receive increased investment.
t.Semmerholm: Semmerholm would gain increased investment for the Quest Against the Vallorn, but only if the Dawnish Assembly named the fight against the Vallorn their highest calling.
t.Weirwater: Weirwater would gain increased investment for the Quest Against the Vallorn, but only if the Dawnish Assembly named the fight against the Vallorn their highest calling.

r.Astolat/Grovesyard: The Nightingale Chorus wayhouse was to be built at Brightway in Grovesyard.

Construct Publishing Clearing House.d: Taddea Ginori invited the Holberg College of Engineering to build Katarzyna von Carstein's designs. The work was funded by six Tassato guilds: the Camorra Barossa, the Gilded Horn, the Jolly Jackdaws, Oathwright Press, the Silver Rivers Casino and the Printers' Guild. It required 50 wains of white granite, 150 crowns in labour and three months to build. Its custodian, the Printmaster of the Publishers' Exchange, was to be appointed by League Bourse Auction, and this election method drew extended scrutiny. Citizens contributed granite and money after the Summer Solstice and the Autumn Equinox. Once complete, it would raise Tassato business income by 36 rings and lift the Printmaster of Cevia's income to two thrones.

n.The League: A League Chair of the Wolf announced the work, the guilds of Tassato paid for it, and a new League title would be sold by Bourse Auction, intended to make a League city the printing centre of the Empire and its neighbours.

t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: the Holberg College of Engineering was invited to build the Clearing House to Katarzyna von Carstein's designs.
t.Tassato: Once complete, the Clearing House would increase the income of businesses in Tassato by 36 rings and cement the city as the Empire's centre of printing.

r.Tassato/Tassato Mestra: Tassato Mestra was the site chosen for the Great Publishers' Clearing House, and contributions of granite and coin towards its construction were recorded through the Autumn Equinox.

Construct Red Wind Wharfs.d: Proposed by Eulàlia i Phovas i Riqueza, Senator for the Madruga, and seconded by Garviel i Abrira i Erigo, Senator for Feroz, the motion followed the opportunity set out in the Mermaids in the basement wind of fortune. The edifice was to cost 5 wains of mithril and 15 crowns in labour and take three months to build. After the Summer Solstice, Gisli i Phovas i Guerra provided 1 throne, 7 crowns and 5 wains of weirwood towards it. Once finished, any army with the Forayer quality can move normally between Free Landing and the mainland, ignoring the island quality, while the upkeep of the Municipal Docks rises by one throne.

n.The Brass Coast: Brass Coast senators for Madruga and Feroz proposed and seconded the motion, and a Brass Coast citizen funded the work. The finished wharfs would give Forayer armies easier movement to and from Free Landing in their home territory.

t.Madruga: Madruga, then divided between the Iron Confederacy and the Brass Coast, gained a new edifice at the Calvos docks that would open Free Landing to Forayer armies without the hindrance of its island quality.

r.Madruga/Calvos Sound: The Red Wind Wharfs were to be built onto the Municipal Docks at Calvos in Calvos Sound, raising the docks' upkeep by one throne.
r.Madruga/Free Landing: Once the wharfs are complete, armies with the Forayer quality can move normally between Free Landing and the mainland, ignoring the island quality.

Construct Sakari's Legacy.d: Invoking Adamant's Aid, an opportunity linked to the Sound and vision Wind of Fortune, the Master of the Koboldi announced a fortification named Sakari's Legacy in Anduzjasse. The boon makes it a rank two fortification that is unbreakable and quicker to raise. It costs 180 wains of white granite and 540 crowns in labour, with twelve months listed for construction. After the Summer Solstice and Autumn Equinox of 388YE, contributions of granite and money came from various citizens, led by Isario i Riqueza with 52 wains of granite and 3 thrones, and Cosme i Zuhri i Guerra with 3 wains and 11 thrones. Once complete, the fortification will have its bastion in Anduzjasse.

n.The Brass Coast: Many Freeborn, especially of the Riqueza and Guerra families, gave granite and money towards a permanent, unbreakable rank two fortification to defend their homeland of Segura.

t.Segura: Segura is to gain Sakari's Legacy, an unbreakable rank two fortification that will strengthen the territory's defences once complete.

r.Segura/Anduzjasse: Anduzjasse was chosen as the site of the bastion of Sakari's Legacy, with construction under way and funded through 388YE.

Construct Smugglers Cove in Tromsa Summe.d: The motion arose from the Beneath a Moonless Sky Wind of Fortune. The commission required 14 wains of white granite, 42 crowns in labour costs and three months to complete. After the Summer Solstice, Rahmah i Darwisj i Erigo provided 3 thrones 5 crowns and Rhys Nighthaven provided 1 crown. After the Autumn Equinox, Rahmah provided 10 wains of white granite. The page does not record whether the cove was finished. Once complete, fleets from across the Empire would be able to take the Scout Smugglers Cove in Tromsa voyage, and Wintermark fleets would gain the Sail into the Cold voyage.

n.Jotun: The Senate commissioned an Imperial smugglers' cove in Tromsa, a territory the Jotun held at the time, giving Imperial fleets a new way to scout its coast.
n.Wintermark: Once the cove is complete, Wintermark fleets will gain access to the Sail into the Cold voyage, an opportunity open only to them.

t.Tromsa: A smugglers' cove was commissioned in Jotun-held Tromsa, which would let Imperial fleets take the Scout Smugglers Cove in Tromsa voyage once it was complete.

Construct Statue of Murdered Researchers.d: Ada Droon Drifting Bough, as Mistress of Monuments, announced an edifice in Apulus to honour researchers murdered by the Whisper Gallery, with the consent of the Senator for Apulian. Ignacio i Zuhri i Erigo was to fund it fully. The cost was 3 wains of mithril, 1 wain of weirwood, 1 wain of white granite and 15 crowns in labour, with three months to build. After the Summer Solstice Ignacio provided all the materials, and Firesong Arachas, Fiorente Vicente d'Apulian and Rhys Nighthaven contributed money towards the labour. Once complete, a statue will be raised in Apulus.

n.The League: A memorial to researchers murdered by the Whisper Gallery is to stand in the League's territory of Spiral, approved by the Senator for Apulian and largely funded by Ignacio i Zuhri i Erigo.

t.Spiral: Spiral is to gain a statue honouring the researchers killed by the Whisper Gallery, to be raised in Apulus once its three-month construction is complete.

r.Spiral/Apulus: Apulus is the site of the planned statue to the murdered researchers. The materials were supplied after the Summer Solstice, with money contributed towards the labour, and the statue is to be raised once construction is complete.

Construct Wayward House.d: Paris of Apulus, Bearer of an Imperial Wayleave, announced the commission of the Wayward House in Apulian, in Apulus, Spiral. It was to be built by the Edificer's Guild of Apulian, with funding from Damian i Martan i Erigo. The work required twelve wains of white granite and 36 crowns in labour, and would take three months to build. After the Summer Solstice 388YE, Paris of Apulus provided 4 thrones 4 crowns and the twelve wains of white granite. Once complete, the apartments will house Jarmish pilgrims of the Way who visit the Empire.

n.The League: League citizens drove the project: a Bearer of an Imperial Wayleave, Paris of Apulus, announced it and paid for it, Damian i Martan i Erigo funded it, and the Edificer's Guild of Apulian is building it in a League city.

t.Spiral: Spiral gains a new white granite edifice in Apulian, meant to welcome Jarmish pilgrims of the Way into the territory.

r.Spiral/Apulus: The Wayward House apartments are going up in the city of Apulian in Apulus, using twelve wains of white granite over three months, and will host visiting Jarmish pilgrims.

Construct Wrangler's Market.d: Senator Ana i Taziel i Riqueza of Segura proposed the motion, seconded by Senator Eulàlia i Phovas i Riqueza of Madruga. It sought 14 wains of weirwood or 64 thrones, and passed at 54 thrones, which were disbursed to the Senator for Segura. The work also required 42 crowns in labour and three months to complete. After the Summer Solstice, Tancred Enrico i Taziel i Riqueza provided 5 thrones and the 14 wains of weirwood. Farren Silver Streams and Rhys Nighthaven each gave a crown. Once complete, fleet owners would appoint a Chief Wrangler by Freeborn tally, and Imperial Orc military units could use the market to spy on Arbonne.

t.Bay of Catazar: The market was to be built in Arbonne, beyond Imperial control, so that once finished Imperial Orc military units could use it to spy on Arbonne.

Construct Wyrding Tower.d: Announced by Borys Vardovich Straskovich, Boyar of the Iron Roads, the commission built a ministry proposed in an appraisal by Graciana i Lopez i Guerra, linked to the Sunrise over Livardz wind of fortune. The commission spoke of bringing prosperity to the ruins left by the Cold Sun. It required 12 wains of mithril, 36 crowns in labour and three months' work. After the Summer Solstice, Emil Artemov Lenka and Yaroslav Goraschenko Vernost each supplied six wains of mithril, with coin given by several citizens. On completion, the title Volhov of the Wyrding Tower became available, chosen by tally of Varushkan mine and forest owners from the Autumn Equinox 388YE, and the ashen wind's threat was lifted.

n.Varushka: Varushka gained a new volhov tower and the title Volhov of the Wyrding Tower, to be appointed by the votes of Varushkan mine and forest owners from the Autumn Equinox 388YE.

t.Volodmartz: The tower's completion in Volodmartz removed the threat of the ashen wind and was meant to bring prosperity to lands ruined by the Cold Sun.

r.Volodmartz/Livardz: The Wyrding Tower was raised in Livardz, among the ruins left by the Cold Sun, and its completion ended the threat of the ashen wind there.

Construct the Northern Way.d: Announced by the Master of Rings and so carrying the support of League citizens, the Northern Way cost 50 wains of white granite, 30 wains of mithril and 30 thrones in labour, and took six months to construct. After the Summer Solstice, Bella di Sarvos supplied the largest share of materials and money, with further granite from League citizens, mithril from Leofric d'Apulian and crowns from several others. Once complete it raises investment in Zenith by one, giving each business there 36 rings, removes the Black Plateau's penalty to Spiral's businesses, and lets the Crucible of Fate boost the Legacy's output and upgrade personal resources.

n.The League: The great work was announced by a League Master of Rings, gained the backing of League citizens, and lifts the Black Plateau's burden on businesses in Spiral, a League territory.
n.Urizen: The Northern Way links Apulian with the Urizen territory of Zenith, raising investment there so that every business in Zenith gains 36 rings once it is complete.

t.Spiral: The Northern Way is built in Spiral, and once complete it removes the penalty that the Black Plateau places on businesses in the territory.
t.Temeschwar: Mentioned in passing: the motion was announced by Laughlan Vi Temeschwar, whose name refers to the territory.
t.Zenith: Zenith is the destination of the safe passage from Apulian, and its investment level rises by one, providing 36 rings for each business there.

r.Spiral/Apulus: The great work is constructed at the city of Apulian in Apulus, creating a safe route north towards Zenith.

Everything is on show.d: The Senate approved the army at the Winter Solstice 386YE on Cesare's motion, seconded by Aspar, with most of the funding from Empress Vesna Borkovna Prochnost. Eighteen months later, its recruits from all five League cities were finishing at the Five Cities Military Academy. Cesare could choose Conquering, Fast or Resourceful at no extra cost, and the army gained the Resourceful quality, letting it resupply anywhere, even under attack. Its creation swelled Pride in Tassato, whose new army would rival Holberg's Towerjacks and the Wolves of War. Lingering effects of the Hammers of Fury enchantment also made the Chain shine over Tassato, giving local artisans and cambions brief benefits at the summit.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: the Gryphon's Pride, raised as conquerors for Dawnish ambitions in the Barrens, was cited as the model for the Conquering option, which was not chosen.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Towerjacks are remembered for spending three decades on Holberg's walls keeping the Druj out.
n.The League: The League gained its third army, the Sparrows Reckoning, drawn from all five cities and made Resourceful. Its ambitious, hot-headed soldiers are eager to prove themselves the equals of the Wolves of War and the Towerjacks.

t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: Holberg's fame for the Towerjacks' thirty-three-year siege is the reputation Tassato's proud citizens now hope their new army will rival.
t.Tassato: Tassato gained its first army of its own, swelling the city's Pride. Lingering Hammers of Fury magic made the Chain shine brightly overhead, letting local artisans refresh a bonded item and cambions gain a temporary hero point at the summit.
t.The Barrens: Mentioned in passing: Dawnish ambitions in the Barrens are referred to as the reason the Gryphon's Pride were raised as conquerors.

Full circles.d: While helping resist Cold Sun in Jarm, Sevenfold Path magicians grew close to the Convocation of Virtue, a structureless fellowship of Jarmish pilgrims. A Conclave declaration brought by Damiàn i Martàn i Erigo, rather than Grandmaster Elagabala, sent them a gift of liao, and magistrates are investigating it as possible subversion. The Convocation honours Vasilia the Pilgrim as its spiritual founder and offered to share her story if invited for historical research. It proposed a House of the Pilgrim on the Bay of Catazar coast to host Jarmish pilgrims, offering four Jarmish star jewels in return. The Wayward House was commissioned in Spiral, and the Grandmaster successfully guided the order towards closer ties.

n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: the accompanying story follows Nevyn, a Navarr vate, dining with a Jarmish magician after campaigning together against Cold Sun.
n.The League: The Wayward House, a shrine offering hospitality to Jarmish pilgrims of the Way, was commissioned in the League's territory of Spiral. The page also compares the Convocation's sect leaders to League bishops.

t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: the Convocation asked that the House of the Pilgrim be built in a coastal region on the Bay of Catazar.
t.Spiral: Spiral became home to the Wayward House, commissioned to welcome Jarmish pilgrims visiting the Empire's sites of virtue and meeting Imperial followers of the Way.

In the Court of Far Horizons.d: Magistrate Abraham's analysis found the manifesto covered maritime trade only. Overland trade, and fleet espionage or warfare, fell outside it. If passed, the sodality would gain the power to set tariffs, though the Court advised softening the 'never hindered' wording. Five titles would automatically become sodality appointments, and others, including Bourse seats and most ambassadors, could be transferred by Senate motion. The Fellowship of the Purple Sails would join en masse and share docking rights at Hayden if tariffs were granted. The Bedelaar Huisbaas offered up to 12 thrones a season for control of trade titles. The City of Salt and Sail offered a yearly message to anyone if the sodality appointed all ambassadors.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the leader of a named Druj sept is given as an example recipient of the City of Salt and Sail's yearly message.
n.Grendel: The Grendel are named as a mercantile power for whom trade matters in foreign relations. The Ambassador to the Grendel is among the posts the Senate could transfer to the new sodality, despite the ongoing war mentioned at Caricomare's docks.
n.The League: Caricomare's rebuilt docks frame the story, as Fleet Master Giovanni von Temeschwar receives word from the Purple Sails. The Mayor of Caricomare could become a sodality appointment, and the Merchant Prince of Misericorde Market would come under a broader trade sodality.
n.Thule: The Empire's extensive trade with the Thule of Otkodov is entirely overland, so it falls outside the proposed remit. The Ambassador to Otkodov is the one envoy the sodality could not be given.

t.Holberg: Overland trade with the Sand Fishers of Holberg lies outside the maritime manifesto. It would come under the sodality only if the manifesto were broadened to cover all foreign trade.
t.Otkodov: Imperial trade with Otkodov involves no fleets, which is why its ambassador is excluded from any transfer to the Court of Far Horizons.

r.Holberg/Misericorde: Mentioned in passing: the Merchant Prince of Misericorde Market is listed among the overland trade titles that would need re-evaluation if the sodality's remit were widened to all foreign trade.

In the charnel pit.d: Heilyn Bronwen's Rest's calling let the Prosperity Assembly name a territory each summit for a year, leading to costly chances to help it rebuild. Ada of House Meliora's Courage calling sought to free those scarred by Druj auras of fear. The Silent Bell report on fear, held by Earl Adel de Òrdraig and Gaelen Embercast, would be published by the Autumn Equinox, and a lecture, 'Courage in Convalescence', would gather accounts from formerly oppressed peoples. Supporters of the Proffered Hand proposed First Light Refuge at Hope's Rest. Esther urged a General Assembly mandate to let Druj fear-craft die with them; without a greater majority, Wintermark, Varushka and Urizen could still pursue it.

n.Dawn: The proposed First Light Refuge would be built at Hope's Rest in the Dawnish-held Barrens, serving as the first stop for people escaping or rescued from the Druj.
n.Druj: The Druj's methods of creating auras of fear are the subject of a Silent Bell report and of a debate over whether the Empire should seek the secret lore of the Buruk Tepel or let it die with them.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Grendel is not named directly; Grendel-held Feroz is cited as still in poverty after Governor Rahab's rule, and roughly a thousand people were rescued from Leen.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: Thule-held Otkodov is listed among lands where the Empire might one day build further refuges if it sought to liberate their people.
n.Urizen: If Esther's mandate passes without a greater majority, Urizen would still gain chances to acquire the skills of the Buruk Tepel.
n.Varushka: Varushka would be unaffected by Esther's proposed mandate unless it passes with a greater majority, keeping open its chances to learn the Buruk Tepel's skills.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark would retain the chance to acquire Buruk Tepel lore unless Esther's mandate to forgo it is enacted with a greater majority.

t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: the Freeborn and other nations on the Bay of Catazar are helping roughly a thousand people rescued from Leen come to terms with their ordeal.
t.Feroz: Feroz is named as still languishing in poverty after Governor Rahab's corrupt rule, making it a possible focus for the Prosperity Assembly's aid.
t.Otkodov: Mentioned in passing: Otkodov is listed among lands on whose borders new refuges might be built if the Empire ever sought to liberate their people.
t.Salt Flats of Sanath: Mentioned in passing: the territory is not named; the page refers only generally to eastern lands left in ruins by the Druj and to peoples learning to live free of miasma.
t.Sarangrave: Ada of House Meliora's calling explicitly aims to liberate the sept of the Sarangrave from their cruel Druj captors by learning to combat auras of fear.
t.The Barrens: A charitable edifice, First Light Refuge, was proposed for Hope's Rest in the Barrens to receive and outfit ex-Druj people, costing 12 white granite and 36 crowns with an upkeep of six thrones a season.

r.The Barrens/Hope's Rest: Hope's Rest was proposed as the site of First Light Refuge, a hub of the Proffered Hand Network close to the Mallum, overseen by a new Lantern Keeper appointed by the Courage Assembly.

Invest in Beoraidh Docks.d: Bloodcrow Rasp, Senator for Skarsind, proposed the motion and Rane Shardbearer, Senator for Kallavesa, seconded it. It passed at 75 thrones, which were disbursed to the Senator for Skarsind. The edifice required 30 wains of weirwood, 90 crowns in labour and three months to build. After the Summer Solstice, Pathfinder Gaddak, Zaccaria di Sarvos and Farren Silver Streams contributed money. After the Autumn Equinox, Bloodcrow Rasp and Karrak supplied the 30 wains of weirwood. Once complete, the docks would open Beoraidh to Imperial fleet captains, raise taxation in Mareave by three thrones and raise tariffs by seven thrones. Further background appears in the Each ages a lens wind of fortune.

n.Grendel: The docks were to be built at Beoraidh, a port the Grendel held at the time, and would open it to Imperial fleet captains for trade.

t.Mareave: Once complete, the new docks would raise taxation in Mareave by three thrones and bring a further seven thrones in tariffs.

r.Mareave/Beoraidh: Beoraidh was the site of the commissioned docks, which would open its port to Imperial fleet captains for prosperous trade.

Keys of Enlightenment.d: Sumaah sought Imperial mithril and weirwood for its war with the Asaveans. The City of Salt and Sail offered to carry at least a hundred wains until the end of Winter 388YE, if Ambassador Accalon named a price. Oxtitocszin sent an essay on the paragon Sjördeyr and offered scholars for historical research. The Republic doubted the Liberty Pact could survive without the Commonwealth and feared an Imperial–Axou voting bloc. The true liao gift will continue. The ship Tumlare, struck by an unknown malady, needs aid from the Hand of Guerra. Agent Vassa's network vanished, and several possible investigations were offered, most needing Albrecht von Holberg's cooperation.

n.Highguard: Ambassador Accalon of Highguard was asked to name a price and volume for mithril and weirwood wains, and the Sjördeyr enquiry he received came from the Senator of Bastion.
n.The League: The League's Regario Dossier, held by Albrecht von Holberg, lost its Zemeh spy network, and League ship-captains could join a special scouting voyage to Zemeh if the Spymaster arranged one.

t.Tassato: Mentioned in passing: the Regario Dossier's offices in Tassato Regario received the sole ciphered warning that the Zemeh network had been rolled up.

r.Tassato/Tassato Regario: The Regario Dossier's offices here received a single genuine-seeming ciphered message reporting dead and vanished agents in Zemeh, and their contact attempts since have gone unanswered.

Love and monsters.d: With the Barrens won and the Druj crumbling, Dawn turned to the vallorn. Several opportunities were offered. One was a grand monument in Murderdale that would halve the cost of enlarging Dawnish armies until the vallorn is defeated. Another was a pair of competing Synod mandates: one supporting the Vallornguard's leadership of the Knight of the Greenwood, the other pressing a Dawnish claim on Brocéliande. A third was the Gardens of the Sphinx in Weaving, which would trade a college of magic for an army of war witches. Eleonaris also summoned General Katelyn. Lord Reynard Griffinsong's Vallornguard mandate was upheld, so an administrative motion was due at the Autumn Equinox 388YE. Katelyn met Eleonaris, but the details remain unclear.

n.Dawn: Dawn's Assembly embraced the vallorn as its Highest Calling and backed the Vallornguard to lead questing from Greenwood Manor. Opportunities remained for a monument to cheapen enlarging Dawnish armies and for gardens that would let Dawn raise a war-witch army.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are described as beaten and crumbling, with Dawnish folk debating whether to finish them or turn on the vallorn.
n.Navarr: Navarr had already embraced the Vallornguard, and Dawn chose to follow suit rather than enact the rival mandate that would have pressed a Dawnish claim on Brocéliande, a vallornheart territory Navarr would regard as its concern.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: the Citadel Guard is cited as the only rival to Dawnish war witches in battlefield magic.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: Dawnish characters recall the conquest of Ossium as one of the Empire's victories over the Druj.

t.Astolat: The Gardens of the Sphinx could be built in Weaving, giving up a Dawnish college of magic so that Dawn could raise another army built around war witches.
t.Brocéliande: A competing mandate would have sent Dawnish nobles and yeofolk into Brocéliande and raised Dawn's banner there, but the Assembly upheld the rival Vallornguard mandate instead.
t.Morrow: Mentioned in passing: Morrow is not named, though the page notes that three vallornhearts lie adjacent to the Barrens.
t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: in the opening dialogue, Ossium is recalled as conquered from the Druj.
t.Sarangrave: Mentioned in passing: Sarangrave's conquery is cited as a joint victory with Eleonaris to be celebrated with a triumph, and as an example that a vallornheart territory need not be Navarr land.
t.The Barrens: Now held by Dawn and bordered by three vallornhearts, the Barrens could host a vast monument in Murderdale to rally Dawnish soldiers against the vallorn.

r.Brocéliande/Boar's Dell: Dawnish yeofolk would have settled in Boar's Dell under the competing Brocéliande mandate, which was not the one the Assembly upheld.
r.The Barrens/Murderdale: Murderdale was offered as the site of The Vallorn's Demise, a statue costing 75 white granite, 225 crowns and a dose of true liao that would halve the cost of enlarging Dawnish armies until the vallorn is defeated.

Mark of the Ravadi.d: The Vigilance Assembly recognised Ravadi Founders' Dance as an exemplar in 386YE, authorised a memorial in 387YE and chose Madruga for it in Spring 388YE. Ravadi died fighting the Dry Patricians in the old Great Grasses, but that spot now lies in the Quiet Grasses, where lingering Winter magic prevents an inspirational site. Instead the Custodes Clavicum offered the labour for Ravadi's Bow at Lightsea, a home and training keep for future Champions of Vigilance. The Senate could commission it without using one of its limited commissions, for 10 white granite and 5 mithril. If it is consecrated with true liao, it gives the Champion of Vigilance a permanent income of 24 ingots. Once in the following year, the Vigilance Assembly could also mandate the Champion to lead a new venture against a named threat.

n.Dawn: Ravadi was born Ravadi Watcher to House Berinore of Dawn, served House Castellan as a retainer and fought as a marksman in the Golden Sun before leaving to stride with the Navarr.
n.Navarr: Ravadi swore a Binding of Thorns and joined the Founders' Dance striding, walking the original path of Navarr and Thorn against the vallorn. Their partners in the Great Dance were Nathair Autumngale and the later blasphemer Fintan Nighthaven.
n.The Brass Coast: The memorial keep was proposed for Lightsea in Madruga, giving the Brass Coast territory a potential site of pilgrimage and a permanent home for the Champions of Vigilance.

t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: Ravadi's remains are presumed to have been washed into the Catazar by the flood, and the Wreckers once used a Siakha-powered maelstrom in Madruga to launch assaults across the Bay.
t.Madruga: The Vigilance Assembly chose Madruga, where Ravadi fell fighting the Dry Patricians, for the memorial. The potent and dangerous magic lingering there shaped where the keep could be built.

r.Madruga/Crucible: Mentioned in passing: the wild, uncontrolled Crucible, formed when the Great Grasses were split, is described as a nexus of the realms of Adversity and their most dangerous magic.
r.Madruga/Lightsea: Lightsea was the proposed site of Ravadi's Bow, a small keep housing and training future Champions of Vigilance, to be built if the Senate commissioned it by the end of the Summer Solstice.
r.Madruga/Quiet Grasses: The exact spot where Ravadi fell lies in the Quiet Grasses, but the lingering touch of Winter magic means no inspirational location can currently be created there.

Mithril and rope.d: The Summer Storm, Towerjacks, Argent Sword and Wolves of War defended Clisearn alongside Rucraic's Redoubt and Summer-realm heralds from three magical fortresses, while the Rivers of Life healed wounds overnight on both sides. The Storm Sharks led the Grendel assault, and the Black Eels, Bone Nautilus and Hamsin stole the season's 24 wains of Fundindelve mithril. The Argent Sword and Wolves of War intercepted the raiders and recovered much of it. The violet-sailed Katabat, a fifth Grendel navy bearing Urizeni lightstones, and an Asavean flotilla turned the tide. The Grendel now stand three-quarters of the way to taking Clisearn; the Empire lost over a thousand soldiers. Several battle opportunities followed.

n.Grendel: Grendel armies led by the Storm Sharks advanced three-quarters of the way to seizing Clisearn and raided the Fundindelve, and they raised the new Katabat navy with Asavean help, though they may have suffered up to twice the Empire's casualties.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Summer Storm and the garrison of Rucraic's Redoubt fought hard to hold Clisearn but were pushed back. Orcs with resources in Mareave may have gained a boon from Cathan Canae, and the Uthni offered a bounty against the Grendel healer Leagsaidh.
n.The League: The Towerjacks helped contain the Grendel advance while the Wolves of War plundered the enemy and recovered stolen mithril. League citizens were also offered the chance to hire the Ilium Jackals and to release the Spiteri Bequest.
n.Urizen: The Argent Sword marched to Mareave to plunder the Grendel and helped intercept the Fundindelve raiders. Urizeni scouts noted with concern that the Katabat bears Urizeni lightstones and may draw on lore stolen from Redoubt.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: Varushkans acting for the general of the Boyar's Hasta were named as able to hire the Ilium Jackals mercenaries.

t.Bay of Catazar: The Grendel completed a fifth navy, the violet-sailed Katabat, on the Bay, and the Asavean Plenum sent more warships there to fight the Empire.
t.Mareave: Mareave saw ferocious fighting under the Rivers of Life, and the Grendel drove the defenders back across Clisearn while Beoraidh stayed neutral. The Empire lost over a thousand soldiers, and the Grendel perhaps twice as many.
t.Redoubt: There was concern that the Katabat drew inspiration and power from magical resources stolen from Redoubt during the recent Grendel invasion.
t.Sarvos: A necklace looted when the Grendel sacked Sarvos was located with a Grendel maistir in Mareave, and its return would release the Spiteri Bequest and a trading schooner.
t.Spiral: Imperial armies marched south through Spiral, and a Grendel maistir was recruiting mercenaries to raid the Legacy, which the Custodian of the Legacy was charged to stop.
t.Zenith: Mentioned in passing: the Winter Sun withdrew to Zenith along with the Seventh Wave.

r.Mareave/Beoraidh: The city state of Beoraidh stayed neutral, and its fortification, the Palace of Chains, aided neither side.
r.Mareave/Clisearn: Clisearn was the main battlefield: the Grendel came within a quarter of taking it, held back only by Iskander's Donjon. The Fundindelve was stripped of mithril, though it and the Grand Lodge stayed in Imperial hands, and a battle loomed at the Ruins of Sinat.
r.Mareave/Eoradal: The Summer Storm passed through Eoradal, where they were joined by the orc soldiers of the enchanted bastion Rucraic's Redoubt, whose ranks were swelled by northern Mareave volunteers.
r.Mareave/Fleisardh: Grendel navies, including the new Katabat, gathered off the coast of Grendel-held Fleisardh, and the Fundindelve raiders raced to reach its safety.
r.Mareave/Icarion: A Frozen Citadel of white marble and blue ice, garrisoned by pale-eyed elfin warriors of the Summer realm, rose in Icarion.
r.Mareave/Nadir: A Frozen Citadel of ice with six iron minarets, manned by Summer-realm archers, rose over Nadir.

Myth makers.d: Morajasse's Grendel, recognised as foreigners under Commander Gallum Fiersach, asked to deal through Imperial Consul Atte Arrow-Tongue Metsastajason. The Spice Gardens of Feroz reopened under Sadiq i Isa i Erigo, and orc soldiers helped restore farms. A delegation met the requested citizens at Anvil, and the Freeborn Assembly upheld with a greater majority a statement encouraging trade with the Protectorate. The Thule still invited Imperial help against the Druj, but no armies joined. Their Ambassador met Runa at the Aureate Jetty. Beoraidh, under Sarcophan protection, held talks with Skoura, traded salt for Unshackled beef, and gained Senate-commissioned docks. The Gull Isle shrine was consecrated to Loyalty. Speaker Morna derided Starlight Starchaser but promised a private reply.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: Dawn sends food shipments north to feed Otkodov's people and armies under the treaty with the Thule.
n.Druj: The Thule continued their invasion of the Forest of Ulnak against the Druj, offering crystal mana to Imperial warbands who aided the Earthquake Drummers, though no Imperial armies joined the campaign.
n.Grendel: Speaker Morna sarcastically dismissed Starlight Starchaser as an ambassador without a palace but promised a private reply, while the orcs of Morajasse and Beoraidh both stood apart from the Grendel.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: the Ambassador to Beoraidh is the Highborn Melkior of Balthazar's Vineyard, who warned Ehsan about the Rivers of Life, assured him of dock funding and cautioned him about the Sarcophan Delves.
n.Imperial Orcs: Frith of the Unshackled serves as Advisor on Orc Affairs, and a new trading post exchanging Beoraidh salt for Unshackled beef brought prosperity to Skarsind's herds.
n.Jotun: The Jotun remained at war with the Empire, yet three ghodi came to Gull Isle to witness the consecration of the Virtuous shrine to Loyalty and discuss what the aura means to the Empire.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: Navarr helps ship food to Otkodov, and the Great Forest Orcs are said to regard the Navarr as close allies.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn regained the Spice Gardens and reopened farms in Morajasse, Feroz figures met the Protectorate's delegation at Anvil, and the Freeborn Assembly upheld with a greater majority a call to trade with the Protectorate.
n.The Marches: Mentioned in passing: free Jotun thralls of the Marches are noted as an orc community within the Empire, and the Jotun invasion of Mitwold is said to have only just ended.
n.Thule: Otkodov stayed at peace with the Empire while waging war on the Druj in Ulnak, met the Imperial Ambassador at the Aureate Jetty, and had warlocks watch Imperial pilgrims heading to the Maze of Zoria.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: the Ambassador to the Grendel, mocked by Speaker Morna, is Starlight Starchaser of Urizen.
n.Varushka: Varushkan wise ones travelled through Thule lands to the Maze of Zoria to learn about the face-peelers' creature and were watched by silent Thule warlocks.
n.Wintermark: Winterfolk led much of the diplomacy: Consul Atte and Ambassador Kindra Surefoot dealt with the orc nations, and Erlend led the consecration of the shrine at the Gull Isle Meeting Place.

t.Bregasland: Mentioned in passing: listed as one of the Imperial lands under Jotun control.
t.Feroz: The Spice Gardens returned to the Brass Coast, farms reopened in Morajasse, and the Protectorate guarding Feroz's borders pursued a treaty, though many locals still kept the orcs at arm's length.
t.Forest of Ulnak: The Thule invasion of Ulnak against the Druj continued under Tathenon the Gyre, with Imperial warbands welcome to join, though no Imperial armies did after the Summer Solstice.
t.Kallavesa: The Virtuous shrine at the Meeting Place on Gull Isle, an ancient place of exchange between the ancestors of the Jotun and the Kallavesi, was consecrated to Loyalty with true liao.
t.Liathaven: Mentioned in passing: named as under Jotun control, with the Jotun calling it Ashvale.
t.Mareave: Beoraidh, in Mareave, opened a salt-for-beef trading post, saw the Senate commission docks, held talks with Skoura in Eoradal, and arranged a meeting with the Brine Turtles of Fleisardh.
t.Miekarova: Mentioned in passing: not named directly; the related Varushkan pilgrimage crossed Thule lands to reach the Maze of Zoria under the treaty.
t.Mitwold: Mentioned in passing: the recent Jotun invasion of Mitwold is said to have only just ended.
t.Otkodov: Otkodov stayed at peace with the Empire, hosted Imperial pilgrims to the Maze of Zoria under Thule watch, and sent Runa to meet the Ambassador on an agenda including the Vallorn and the war in the Mallum.
t.Redoubt: Mentioned in passing: not named directly; Urizen appears only as the nation of Ambassador Starlight Starchaser.
t.Segura: Mentioned in passing: some politically engaged priests of Segura were aware of the Freeborn statement on trading with the Protectorate.
t.Skarsind: The new salt-for-beef trade with Beoraidh brought prosperity to the Shepherd of the Southern Herd and the Shepherd of the Great Herd.

r.Feroz/Morajasse: Gallum Fiersach's Protectorate held Mora's Rock, reopened farms around the restored Spice Gardens under food quotas, and lost its impoverished quality as orc soldiers helped clear land and dig irrigation.
r.Mareave/Beoraidh: Ehsan, Lord of Sand, accepted Sarcophan protection as the price of survival, gained a salt-for-beef trade, and saw the Senate commission Imperial docks for his free port.
r.Mareave/Eoradal: Eoradal provided neutral ground for guarded but cautiously optimistic talks between Beoraidh and Skoura, attended by a Sarcophan advisor.
r.Mareave/Fleisardh: Ehsan arranged a meeting between Imperial representatives and the Brine Turtles sept of Fleisardh, to include an elder, a warleader and a Grendel advisor.
r.Mareave/Sinfoyard: Goods flowed across barren Sinfoyard's borders through the new trading post, and the Rivers of Life spurred short-lived growth on its farms, with Ehsan hinting at strange crops north of Beoraidh.

No Matter What.d: Acting on an Imperial Orc Assembly mandate, the Sunstorm spent a year studying Feroz. They proposed an Afarjasse Training Camp, costing 16 white granite and 48 crowns. It would create a Drill Sergeant title, train the Winter Sun and Summer Storm for humid regions and end Afarjasse's abandonment. It would also open the way for a Senate appraisal, with Vainakoma Dawnstongue as appraiser, of supplying the Fire of the South from Feroz. Their second plan was a Wranglers Market at Bramar, costing 14 weirwood and 42 crowns. Freeborn cattle trading with the Iron Confederacy would let Sunstorm units spy on Arbonne. This market was commissioned, and its Brass Coast Chief Wrangler is first appointed at the Autumn Equinox 388YE.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: a small orc settlement from the old legion-camp days is noted as still existing in Estcastle.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Grendel is not named on the page and is linked only through its holdings in Feroz and Mareave at the time.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Sunstorm sept repaid Freeborn aid with two proposals. Their Wranglers Market now gives Imperial Orc military units a covert means of spying on the Suranni in Arbonne. A proposed Afarjasse camp would train the Winter Sun and Summer Storm for humid regions under a Sunstorm Drill Sergeant.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn gained a new national title, the Chief Wrangler, appointed by Tally of the Votes, with a ministry trading cattle for orichalcum and weltsilver. They also have the chance to appraise supplying the Fire of the South from Feroz if the training camp is built.

t.Feroz: The Sunstorm studied impoverished Feroz for a year and proposed a training camp and a cattle-market spy network there. The market was funded, while the camp and a later appraisal of Feroz's underpopulation remain open opportunities.
t.Kalino: Now called Arbonne under Suranni rule and unmapped by the Empire, this territory is the target of the newly funded Wranglers Market spy network. Imperial Orc units will travel south with Freeborn herds to watch the Suranni there.
t.Mareave: Freeborn advice helped the Imperial Orcs tackle Mareave's aridity, and this aid prompted the Sunstorm's return favour in Feroz. Many Sunstorm are also looking to settle in Mareave.
t.Segura: Mentioned in passing: the Fire of the South traditionally drew supply from the plains of Segura and Feroz, though lately mostly from the Iron Qanat.
t.Semmerholm: Mentioned in passing: Estcastle is cited as home to a small orc settlement surviving from the legion-camp era.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: many Sunstorm settled in Skarsind when the Senate granted it, and Sunstorm founded the Great Herds there.

r.Feroz/Afarjasse: The Wranglers Market was funded for Bramar, working with the Dhomiro of Afar and drawing on Afar's restored herds. A proposed Sunstorm training camp could also end the region's abandoned status.
r.Feroz/Cazar Straits: Mentioned in passing: the Cazar Straits are noted as now under Suranni control, a daily reminder of the uneasy peace with the Iron Confederacy.
r.Feroz/Morajasse: Mentioned in passing: the martially minded Protectorate of Morajasse might enjoy joint exercises with the Sunstorm, a matter for the Imperial Consul to pursue.
r.Mareave/Icarion: The oasis created in Icarion with expert Freeborn advice was the aid the Sunstorm set out to repay in Feroz.
r.Semmerholm/Estmure: Mentioned in passing: a small orc settlement from the legion-camp days is said still to exist at Estcastle.

Phantasms and foam.d: The Red Wind Corsairs, with allied soldiers from Dawn, the Marches and Urizen, raided and pushed into Siroc Bayou. Day magic helped them cope with its warped time and distance, and they ended about three-fifths of the way to claiming it. Phantasmal soldiers and beasts then began attacking after the Maw of Siakha closed. The Fire of the South returned from Bregasland to guard Quzar. The Wings of Kobol and other Suranni forces took Free Landing, closed the Maw of Siakha and broke the Children of Wrecks. Freeborn corsairs rescued relics from Atalaya, and surviving wreckers fled or planned final attacks on Madruga, the Necropolis and Tassato.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: Dawnish soldiers, used to wild and dangerous places, marched with the Red Wind Corsairs into the bayou.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Druj-held marshes of Sarangrave are contrasted with the Bayou, which does not actively try to kill intruders.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the Corsairs slipped past the Grendel to reach Feroz, phantoms of Grendel haunt the bayou, and Grendel vessels hunt the fleeing wreckers.
n.Highguard: Wreckers carrying a cursed bucket of Siakha's water sailed up the Couros to extinguish the flame of Britta's shrine in the Necropolis, and its Guardian, Neala Blackhawk, was charged with stopping them.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Fire of the South marched home from Bregasland, which the Jotun held at the time.
n.The Brass Coast: Freeborn armies advanced into Siroc Bayou and guarded Quzar, and Freeborn corsairs recovered lost relics of the Founding from Atalaya as the Iron Confederacy took Free Landing, the nation's first home.
n.The League: A wrecker crew led by the Duke of Lies attacked the Sapphire Stairs in Tassato, threatening the Keeper's income and Sarvos' farms, while the guardians of Sarvos killed fleeing pirates.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: Urizeni soldiers, attuned to the bayou's magical resonances, accompanied the Red Wind Corsairs.

t.Bay of Catazar: The only Children of Wrecks to escape fled into the Bay, where Imperial, Grendel and Sarcophan vessels will hunt them, and the remnants vowed to go out bringing ruin to the Empire.
t.Bregasland: Mentioned in passing: the Fire of the South left Bregasland, having fulfilled their loyalty to the Marchers, and marched home.
t.Feroz: The Corsairs put to port here, and the Suranni fleets sailed from Feroz to assault Free Landing; the Iron Confederacy also crushed the wreckers on the islands of Feroz.
t.Kahraman: Mentioned in passing: the Red Wind Corsairs marched through Kahraman, where villagers cheered them and offered cheap food and drink.
t.Madruga: Imperial forces made headway in Siroc Bayou while the Suranni took Free Landing. A magnitude 80 Autumn enchantment lies over the territory, and wreckers threaten to curse it with Thunderous Tread of the Trees.
t.Necropolis: A wrecker sloop carrying a boon of Siakha sailed up the Couros to quench the eternal flame at Britta's shrine; if it was repelled, pilgrims' donations would rise by four crowns a season.
t.Sarangrave: Mentioned in passing: its deadly marshes are compared unfavourably with the less hostile Siroc Bayou.
t.Sarvos: The guardians of Sarvos gave fleeing pirates a fatal welcome, but Sarvos' farms and vineyards stood to lose 36 rings a season if the attack on the Sapphire Stairs succeeded.
t.Segura: Mentioned in passing: the Red Wind Corsairs marched through Segura, cheered by its villages.
t.Tassato: Wreckers flying a crude image of Dumon sailed up the Vassa to clog the Sapphire Stairs with corpses and kelp, and the Keeper Raphael Sanguineo Rezia di Tassato was charged with killing Siakha's heralds.

r.Feroz/Cazar Straits: Mentioned in passing: the Wings of Kobol are noted as the navy that led the earlier assault on Cazar Straits.
r.Madruga/Calvos Sound: A near-catastrophic tempest and massive waves from the battle in Free Landing pounded Calvos Sound, but its Freeborn, used to the sea invading their homes, coped.
r.Madruga/Crucible: The Corsairs hope to retake the Crucible from the Bayou; wreckers carrying 'The Snapping Face' passed through, and part of the Crucible lies under the Echo of Transformation.
r.Madruga/Free Landing: The Iron Confederacy conquered Free Landing with Freeborn help, closing the Maw of Siakha and breaking the Children of Wrecks, while relics of Atalaya were carried to Quzar.
r.Madruga/Lightsea: The Fire of the South took up defensive positions around Quzar to watch for the Iron Confederacy, and the region was battered by the Free Landing tempest.
r.Madruga/Siroc Bayou: The Red Wind Corsairs raided for treasure and got about three-fifths of the way to claiming the wild Bayou, before phantasms of Night magic slowed their advance to a crawl.
r.Sarvos/Bocche: Mentioned in passing: a merchant-prince with vineyards in Bocche promised four wains of weirwood to the Keeper of the Sapphire Stair if the wreckers were repelled.

Pride in the Marches.d: The Lasambrian Jotun fled Mitwold, probably to defend Reinos against the Iron Confederacy. Meade, looted but jubilant, could repair its walls and raise a statue of Tom Drake to bolster the Drakes. The stolen Beater's cup went as tribute to the Fjorknae, whose fearless orc ships now harass Marcher and Wintermark fleets. Appraisals on the Fjorknae, the Gullet and a foot-the-ball league were proposed. In Bregasland, Grey Walkers released at Ullsmere Rock erode Jotun control of Grey Fens. Marchers want to know William Guildenstern's heroic deeds. Consecrating Rebellion's Ridge could reopen the Mournwold senator debate. Marchers would resist any persecution of Marcher orcs, risking civil war. Two Red Walder scions threaten Mitwold landmarks.

n.Jotun: The Lasambrian Jotun withdrew from Mitwold, apparently to defend Reinos, but still hold Bregasland, where Grey Walkers are loosening their grip on Grey Fens. Their Fjorknae kin received Meade's loot and now raid the Gullet by ship.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: a Marcher compares any foot-the-ball league unfavourably with the League's great game.
n.The Marches: Mitwold is freed and Meade can honour Tom Drake, but Marchers face Jotun in Bregasland, Fjorknae raiders at sea, debates over folk heroes and Mournwold's senator, and a near-unanimous resolve to defend Marcher orcs against the Synod.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark fleets escorting the fisherfolk of Westerhal, raiding Kalsea or trading with Caitun suffer from Fjorknae warships in the Gullet, and akhlut trailing those ships trouble the Winterfolk.

t.Bregasland: The Jotun consolidate their hold while the Strong Reeds lie low, a stone of the Ullsmere Rock dolmen has been carried off, and Grey Walkers now haunt Grey Fens.
t.Bryadvik: Mentioned in passing: Imperial fleets mapping the Sea of Snow did not cross the Blood Straits between Bryadvik and Fjorknae.
t.Fjorknae: Its orcs received Meade's stolen treasure as tribute and now sail blood-red warships into the Gullet, yet the Empire knows almost nothing about the island and has no spies within reach.
t.Hordalant: A leg of the Ullsmere Rock dolmen has apparently been dragged here to inspire the Howling Night, and Alsterbo at the Kongegőr's southern end matters to any plan to sever the bridge.
t.Liathaven: Mentioned in passing: the retreating Lasambrian Jotun withdrew south into Liathaven, where Imperial scouts lost track of them.
t.Mitwold: The Jotun abandoned the territory after looting Meade and the Beater's cup; Meade may rebuild its walls with a Tom Drake statue, while Red Walder's scions threaten the Maiden Stone and the Golden Fields of Hay.
t.Mournwold: Rebellion's Ridge stands complete, and its consecration would revive bitter arguments over who appoints the senator, while Mournwold priests propose fining the Marcher orcs rather than persecuting them.
t.Reinos: Mentioned in passing: news of the Iron Confederacy invasion of Reinos is the likely reason the Lasambrian Jotun fled Mitwold.
t.Sea of Snow: Fjorknae warships now prowl the Gullet and northern Sea of Snow, attacking Marcher and Wintermark vessels and possibly stirring the coral husks.
t.Skallahn: The earlier Imperial attack here came close to taking Bjarkey, and the Jotun are now alert to the threat of their jarldoms being cut apart at the Kongegőr.
t.Tromsa: Mentioned in passing: the hylje's proposal would need the smugglers cove at Tromsa re-established before it could be fully realised.
t.Upwold: Mentioned in passing: the loss of the Beater's cup has dampened foot-the-ball enthusiasm in Upwold as well as Mitwold.

r.Bregasland/Gravenmarch: Recovered by the Empire last season, Gravenmarch was unexpectedly left alone by the Jotun, while the Strong Reeds wait in the fens.
r.Bregasland/Grey Fens: Grey Walkers released at Ullsmere Rock haunt the region, harassing Jotun and Marcher households alike and steadily pushing to take the region for themselves.
r.Hordalant/Alsterbo: Holding Alsterbo alone no longer guarantees severing the Kongegőr; the Empire would need both ends of the bridge.
r.Mitwold/Golden Downs: Dusty Cobb leads rebels to burn the Golden Fields of Hay, and the Keeper of the Golden Fields, Nicolas Reaper, must stop him or the Silent Giant will suffer.
r.Mitwold/Maiden Downs: Jyll Longleys and her band march to wreck the Maiden Stone, and Champion of Prosperity Tom Appleseed must stop her or Mitwold's farms lose their profits for months.
r.Mitwold/Meade March: Meade was looted but freed and welcomed the Drakes, and may now repair its walls and raise a statue of Tom Drake.
r.Mitwold/Oddmire: Seized by the Jotun last year, Oddmire and Odd's End were abandoned as the Lasambrians fled before Imperial armies.
r.Mitwold/The Meadows: Reclaimed after the Battle of Wayford, the region lost treasures from Wayford, including the Beater's cup, to the Jotun.
r.Mournwold/Ore Hills: Rebellion's Ridge, honouring the executed leaders of the Ore Hills Rebellion, is complete, and consecrating it would stir the miners' old demands for a voice.
r.Skallahn/Bjarkey: The Empire nearly claimed Bjarkey, but holding the Kongegőr's northern end alone no longer guarantees cutting the bridge.

Propensity to truck, barter, and exchang.d: After fast-moving prices and a change of trading staff angered Imperial merchants at the Spring Equinox, the herald Crown consulted the Urizeni architect Abel the Rounder. The City then made eight contracts available for auction to the highest bidder in the Hall of Worlds. Each had to be fulfilled in full at the same summit, with payment three days later, to keep bulk sales from flooding the market. The City also published guidance on the goods it values, favouring ingots, measures, unique goods, herbs and liao, and said large bulk sales outside contracts would draw lower offers. Heralds were open to becoming patron of the Golden Pyramid or its grand lodge, provided the Archmage of Autumn secured a dedicated plenipotentiary before the end of Spring 389YE.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are not named; their only link is that they held Sarangrave, the territory the heralds' banter calls Abel the Rounder's home.

t.Sarangrave: Mentioned in passing: in the in-character exchange, the herald Patina describes Abel the Rounder as one of Sarangrave's foremost architects and calls it a territory with major investment needs.

Raise Fifth Marcher Army.d: The motion carried the standard cost of 200 wains of mithril and 75 thrones in labour, with twelve months needed to complete the work. After the Summer Solstice 388YE, Henry Birchsmith provided the 200 wains of mithril and 74 thrones 7 crowns, and Tom Keeper of Copperhill gave the final crown. The new army also benefited from Hammers of Fury performed by the Cabal Lyktan during that solstice. Once it is complete, the fifth general of the Marches is to be chosen by unanimous decision of the Marcher senators.

n.The Marches: The Marches gained the commission for a fifth army, paid for largely by its own Senator for Upwold. Its general is to be elected by unanimous decision of the Marcher senators once the army is raised.

t.Upwold: The fifth Marcher army is being raised in Upwold, at the proposal of the territory's own senator, Henry Birchsmith, with twelve months needed to complete it.

Raise Fourth Navarr Army.d: Proposed by Rowyn of the Waystone Path, Senator for Hercynia, and seconded by Thalia of Netherwatch, Senator for Redoubt, the motion passed. It carries standard costs of 200 wains of mithril and 75 thrones in labour, and takes twelve months to complete. Llofir, the Rot Lord, provided support equivalent to fifteen wains of mithril after Gwdihŵ gave the eternal seven hundred and fifty drams of marrowort. Many Navarr individuals contributed mithril and money after the Summer Solstice and Autumn Equinox, Rowyn among them. Once complete, the army's general will be chosen by unanimous decision of the Navarr senators. Further detail appears in The first shot wind of fortune.

n.Navarr: Navarr will gain a fourth army built to fight the vallorn, funded in part by many Navarr donors and by the eternal Llofir, with its general to be elected unanimously by the Navarr senators.

t.Miaren: The new fourth Navarr army is to muster in Miaren once its construction is complete.

r.Miaren/Oakways: Oakways is named as the mustering point for the fourth Navarr army.

Raise Fourth Varushkan Army.d: Proposed by Bronimir, Senator for Ossium, and seconded by Tristan duLac, Senator for Weirwater, the motion passed. Raising the army requires 200 wains of mithril, 75 thrones in labour costs and twelve months to complete, in addition to standard costs. After the Summer Solstice and Autumn Equinox of 388YE, individuals including Vesna Borkovna Prochnost, Alexandrina Ivanova Cherenkov, Dorys Delgorokov and Mayra Zoronova Prochnost contributed mithril and money, though the page records only partial progress towards the total. Once complete, the fourth general of Varushka becomes available for election by unanimous decision of the Varushkan senators.

n.Varushka: Varushka stands to gain a fourth army and a new general, chosen by unanimous decision of its senators, and many Varushkans contributed mithril and coin towards raising it.

t.Karsk: Karsk is where the fourth Varushkan army is to be raised once the twelve months of work and the required mithril and labour are complete.

Seeds of discord.d: Axos took Thornfen, expelled all former Druj subjects into Whisperwood and Kroll, and began salvaging Sephals to rebuild the Tower of the Skink. It asked for a Senate motion letting its slowly forming garrison defend Imperial Sarangrave, hinted at a need for mithril or weirwood, and offered lemuré research for 50 liao. A Grendel crew threatened a grounded Axou ship. Faraden executed Tommasso Triusti, the Asavean embassy left, and Faraden queried the Justice proscription. The Iron Confederacy proposed treaty talks for the Autumn Equinox but would not readily give up Free Landing or Cazar Straits. Tsark invited discussion of Prosperity, and the Marracossans feared prosecution under the Theist Heresy judgement.

n.Druj: Former Druj subjects were thrown out of Thornfen by the Axou, Druj guerillas from the old Tower garrison still harass Axou soldiers there, and the Halls of Maykop are studying how to counter Druj armies supported by the walking dead.
n.Grendel: A Grendel crew landed near a grounded Axou trading ship, and the Quaymaster of the Elosian Docks had to ensure fewer than a dozen of them survived to reach it, with lethal force judged fully justified.
n.Jotun: Faraden was to sign a new peace treaty with the Jotun at the Summer Solstice. The Iron Confederacy, whose invasion of Reinos was apparently faltering, offered mutual recognition of any Jotun land each nation took there.
n.The Brass Coast: The Iron Confederacy held the corsair islands of Free Landing and Cazar Straits and showed no willingness to return them, while Freeborn diplomats, including the new ambassador to Faraden, Mina i Yashum i Riqueza, carried much of the season's diplomacy. The Freeborn Assembly was also asked to reassure the Marracossans.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: Sarvos was suggested as one possible site for dedicated Iron Confederacy markets.
n.The Marches: Mentioned in passing: the Liege of the Five Winds sent thanks to former ambassador Ebenezer of the Marches for his work with Faraden.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: the Thule are listed among the nations to which the Empire has an ambassador.
n.Urizen: Urizen was left to deal with the stateless exiles the Axou drove out of Thornfen into Sarangrave. Urizeni priests were invited to discuss Prosperity with the Tsarkoi adepts in Occursion.
n.Wintermark: Thanmir Hrafnar of Wintermark, ambassador to Axos, handled the Thornfen garrison and lemuré negotiations. The Wintermark scholar Marko Siwarsbairn returned from the Iron Confederacy, angry about Suranni censorship of their research.

t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: the Bay is not named directly and is touched on only through the coastal shipping and island affairs described.
t.Feroz: The Iron Confederacy held the Cazar Straits and refused to discuss returning them. The town of Bramar was floated as a possible Suranni trading enclave.
t.Kalino: The Iron Confederacy accepted that the Empire had no role in the Hand of Dumon curses on Arbonne (Kalino), where Imperial ilium was helping to build a warding temple. Marko Siwarsbairn revealed that a mithril mine there supplies Suranni armies.
t.Madruga: Free Landing remained in Suranni hands with only a costly withdrawal conceivable. The Marracossans of Trajadoz feared the Theist Heresy proscription would cut them off from their Freeborn neighbours.
t.Reinos: The Iron Confederacy's invasion of Jotun-held Reinos appeared to be going poorly. The Dukes offered to recognise any land the Empire took there in exchange for the same recognition.
t.Sarangrave: Axos claimed Thornfen and scattered its expelled inhabitants across the territory. It asked for a Senate motion so its slowly forming garrison could defend Imperial Sarangrave outside Nesustak Forest and Bendol.
t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: Sarvos was suggested as a site for a dedicated market for Iron Confederacy ships.
t.Segura: Mentioned in passing: last season's Suranni request to resupply their Reinos armies through western Segura was recalled as having been refused.
t.Upwold: Mentioned in passing: Upwold is not named on the page; any connection is only indirect.
t.Veroigne: Mentioned in passing: the Suranni ambassador's seat in Chaubrette is said to lie west of Veroigne.
t.Zenith: Adept Camilla of Tsark arrived at the Garden of the Perfect World in Occursion to discuss Prosperity with Imperial citizens, with more Tsarkoi adepts and sages expected to follow.

r.Feroz/Cazar Straits: The Iron Confederacy kept the Cazar Straits, seized from the Children of Wrecks, and said relinquishing them was unlikely to be on the table.
r.Feroz/Fontargenta: The Suranni proposed a trading enclave in the town of Bramar, with a market and a temple to Evra the Smith. This was a proposal only.
r.Madruga/Free Landing: Free Landing remained under Suranni occupation. A withdrawal might in theory be negotiated, but only at a very great price in money or materials.
r.Madruga/Torres: The Freeborn of Torres who have befriended and traded with the Marracossans may fear prosecution under the Theist Heresy proscription, and the Marracossans asked them to speak on their behalf.
r.Sarangrave/Bendol: Mentioned in passing: Bendol was excluded from the area the proposed Axou garrison motion would cover.
r.Sarangrave/Kroll: Mentioned in passing: a few stragglers among the people expelled from Thornfen ended up in Kroll.
r.Sarangrave/Nesustak Forest: Mentioned in passing: Nesustak Forest was excluded from the area the proposed Axou garrison motion would cover.
r.Sarangrave/Thornfen: Thornfen passed fully into Axou hands. Its inhabitants were expelled, Druj guerillas continue to harass the occupiers, Sephals is being stripped for white granite, and a garrison is slowly forming at the Tower of the Skink.
r.Sarangrave/Whisperwood: Most of the orcs and humans the Axou expelled from Thornfen were driven into the Whisperwood, without supplies, shelter or clear legal status.
r.Zenith/Occursion: Tsarkoi Adept Camilla settled at the Garden of the Perfect World to meet Urizeni priests and congregations wishing to discuss Prosperity.

Six sheets to the wind.d: Challengers had to receive the magnitude 30 ritual Challenge the Iron Duke, preferably from a coven that had mastered it, and could enter only one challenge. Past victors had to wait a year, and winners chose a reward from the Dragonforge. In the Challenge of the Domination Sands, challengers and visiting Summer heralds would fight individually for five minutes to hold three fixed markers, scoring a point every ten seconds. The top half of scorers with at least one point would win. In the Challenge of the Swift Seas, overseen by the herald Windward, racers would steer token boats through six checkpoints on a gridded map. The first half to finish would be victorious.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: six Dawnish covens, including Drake's Fire, Phoenix Rising and the Golden Grove, are listed among those that cast Challenge the Iron Duke the previous season.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: the Navarr coven The Eternal Family is listed among those that cast Challenge the Iron Duke the previous season.
n.The Brass Coast: Mentioned in passing: the Brass Coast covens The Glass Mantle and The Tempest Flame are listed among those that cast Challenge the Iron Duke the previous season.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: the Wintermark coven Voices of the Unbound Storm is listed among those that cast Challenge the Iron Duke the previous season.

t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: the in-character vignette shows the herald Curator gleefully shouting nonsense orders aboard a ship sailing along the Bay of Catazar.

Survival.d: Key questions, such as whether a fully roused vallorn can spread beyond its territory, cannot yet be answered. Civilian commissions can now be built inside weirwood groves at double labour cost; the vallorn would deactivate them but not destroy them. The Conclave could interdict new arcane projections to save mana, and the Summer Archmage could seek adamant from Deep Dragon for the Master of the Koboldi. Neighbours know far less than the Empire. Tathenon may trade a ritual protecting against miasma. A controversial idea is to copy the Axou strategy of abandoning and walling off vallorn territories. A weirwood fortification of the Heartwood in Summersend is also proposed.

n.Druj: The Druj inherited the heart of Bendol already contained by Terun wards and maintained them until recently. Their knowledge of the vallorn was stolen from Urizeni spires, and they are seen as unlikely partners in any treaty.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the report doubts the Grendel have ever even encountered the vallorn.
n.Jotun: The Jotun hold Liathaven as Ashvale and use their military strength to manage bursts of vallornspawn. They reportedly secured a boon from Surut of the Thrice-cursed Court, though its purpose is unclear.
n.Navarr: The Navarr's long work against the vallorn underpins existing options, including plans with Holberg in Brocéliande and with Urizen in the Sarangrave. The Great Forest Orcs would cut the cost of fortifying the Heartwood if the Navarr national assembly swore not to use, and to oppose Imperial use of, the Ancestor Slayer's fire.
