n.The League: Mentioned in passing: engineers of Holberg worked with the Navarr on a plan to improve the defensibility of Brocéliande.
n.Thule: The Thule keep the vallornheart of Emrys in Sküld quiescent with their own version of Wither the Seed. Their dragon Tathenon reportedly holds a Day ritual protecting against vallorn miasma that the Empire might negotiate for, and aid from the Tower of the Skink garrison against Bendol would be valuable.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: the Druj stole their vallorn knowledge from Urizeni spires, and recent Navarr work with Urizen produced opportunities to defend the Sarangrave.

t.Brocéliande: Navarr and Holberg engineers drew up a plan to make Brocéliande more defensible by luring the vallorn to a chosen battleground. The territory is also among those the controversial Axou-style strategy would abandon.
t.Hercynia: Hercynia is noted as largely undefended beyond the Grim Pyramid. A weirwood fortification of the Heartwood in Summersend is proposed, though Hercynia is also listed among territories the Axou-style strategy would abandon.
t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: Holberg's engineers joined the Navarr in planning Brocéliande's defences.
t.Liathaven: The Jotun-held part, called Ashvale, is managed through Jotun military strength against occasional vallornspawn. Liathaven is among the territories the Axou-style containment idea would abandon.
t.Miaren: Mentioned in passing: Miaren is noted as fine and excluded from the territories the Axou-style strategy would abandon.
t.Otkodov: The Thule keep the vallornheart of Emrys in Sküld quiescent using their own version of Wither the Seed.
t.Sarangrave: The vallorn reared in the Sarangrave this season. Navarr and Urizeni work has produced opportunities to defend key sites, and relations with Axos are judged pivotal to the damage in the east.
t.Therunin: Mentioned in passing: Therunin is listed among the territories the controversial Axou-style strategy would abandon to the vallorn.

r.Hercynia/Deer's Folly: If the vallornheart of Deer's Folly rouses, a weirwood-grown fortification at the Heartwood might prove more resistant to it, though this is uncertain.
r.Hercynia/Summersend: The proposed Fortify the Heartwood commission would be built here for 80 weirwood and 240 crowns over four seasons, available until Summer Solstice 389YE. The Great Forest Orcs offer to reduce the cost in return for a Navarr oath.
r.Liathaven/Liath's Heart: Occasional bursts of vallornspawn emanate from Liath's Heart, which the Jotun reportedly manage with little difficulty.
r.Otkodov/Sküld: The Thule, long holders of Sküld, keep the vallornheart of Emrys quiescent with their own version of Wither the Seed.
r.Sarangrave/Bendol: The heart of Bendol was contained by ancient Terun wards made with Sadogua's help, which the Druj maintained until recently. Aid from the Thule garrison of the Tower of the Skink against it would be of great value.

The Oran operation.d: The engineers judged that bridging the ilium-laden Scorrero, with a magical marsh on its northern bank, was infeasible. They proposed a caisson road bridge from near Oran to the coast east of ruined Siroc, costing 50 white granite, 15 mithril, 15 weirwood and 96 crowns over six months. It would let armies cross, lift Oranseri's impoverishment and restore the Sunset Roads to Segura. With Senate permission, salvaging the drowned Salt Guard or the abandoned Temple of Balo and the Black Bull would reduce the materials needed. An optional Oran Tollkeeper title and adamant reinforcement via the Stone Dragon were also offered. Both the Assembly of the Way and the Freeborn Assembly upheld exorcism mandates to protect the Salt Guard salvage.

n.Grendel: Former Grendel soldiers now serving the Protectorate offered Grendel caisson techniques for the bridge. Their engineer spoke bitterly of Salt Lords who starve professional soldiers in favour of the navies, which has made these troops adept at salvage.
n.The Brass Coast: The bridge would make the Freeborn nation whole again by reconnecting Feroz with Madruga and restoring Segura's trade. The Freeborn and Way assemblies both upheld mandates sending exorcists to honour the dead of the Salt Guard, while the Kanza family objected to tearing down the temple that once sheltered them.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: the Protectorate engineer Grayune recalled being pinned down by Urizen sentinels, in which soldiers could not simply sail away.

t.Feroz: Oranseri would anchor the proposed bridge, and Feroz's cheap labour keeps the cost low, though some questioned the fairness of this and an option to pay full wages was offered. The bridge was framed as a symbol of Feroz's recovery from Governor Rahab's ruin.
t.Kahraman: Mentioned in passing: ilium washing down from the Kahraman peaks has made the Scorrero's magical wildness linger.
t.Madruga: The bridge would restore army movement and overland trade between Madruga and Feroz. However, Madruga's transfigured northern bank of marsh and haunted grass makes building there very difficult.
t.Segura: By linking to the old white granite road into Segura, the Oran Bridge would restore the Sunset Roads benefits that Segura lost when the Scorrero flooded.

r.Feroz/Fontargenta: Mentioned in passing: Fontargenta is not named on the page and is linked only as part of Feroz, the territory at the centre of the bridge plan.
r.Feroz/Morajasse: The Protectorate of Morajasse supplied the engineers behind the proposal. The optional Oran Tollkeeper's income would rise by 6 crowns a season if Morajasse's impoverished quality were removed.
r.Feroz/Oranseri: The bridge would make landfall near Oran, removing Oranseri's impoverished quality and reviving its paradors. The abandoned Asavean temple in Oran could be torn down for materials, and the Inkworks of Joharra could additionally remove the region's abandoned quality.
r.Madruga/Crucible: Crucible is trackless, marshy and outside Imperial control, so the engineers ruled out bridging there. The Red Wind Corsairs aim to retake it after their raid on the Bayou.
r.Madruga/Quiet Grasses: Mentioned in passing: named as one of the haunted-grass and marsh regions created when the Spring-infused Scorrero transfigured Madruga.
r.Madruga/Siroc Bayou: The bridge's northern end would sit on the coast east of ruined Siroc as the Red Wind Corsairs raided to bring the Bayou under Imperial control. The drowned Salt Guard here could be salvaged for granite, with exorcist mandates upheld to keep the dead at rest.

The Visitation.d: A shipment for the Golden Fleet Salvagemaster caused a commotion when unloaded at Crown's Quay in Necropolis. Irate stewards of the dead from Oreb's Vault harassed and delayed it, so a courier arranged to meet the Salvagemaster on Saturday morning to resolve the dispute. The Magistrates confirmed the goods were his. A letter to an unknown "Marisol i Erigo" from the Sovereign Lords of the City of Bar and Bond was found at the regio and published. Landskeeper Shem announced a rock, paper, scissors tournament in the Hall of Worlds, with proceeds split between the winner, the Academy and Upwold. Wayblade Skana planned to visit the Imperial Orc camp to learn about the executed heretic Bloodcrow Knott, who was later added to the Annals of the Ancestors.

n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Grendel is not named; its only link is that Wayblade Skana comes from Mareave, which Grendel held at the time.
n.Highguard: Stewards of the dead from the chapter house at Oreb's Vault in Necropolis were angered by the Salvagemaster's shipment and harassed and delayed it. The Salvagemaster was asked to placate them, although the Magistrates confirmed the goods were his.
n.The Marches: Landskeeper Shem toured Upwold gathering ribbon for his Anvil tournament. A quarter of the takings would go back with him to help with the problems of being a landskeeper in trying times.

t.Mareave: Wayblade Skana, a preacher from Mareave, was set to travel to the Imperial Orc camp at Anvil to learn about the life and death of Bloodcrow Knott.
t.Necropolis: The Salvagemaster's shipment caused a commotion when it was unloaded at Crown's Quay, and stewards from Oreb's Vault hounded the cart carrying it all the way to Anvil.
t.Upwold: Landskeeper Shem spent the month travelling across Upwold preparing his tournament. A quarter of its proceeds was earmarked to help with the troubles landskeepers faced there.

The brightest flame.d: Nim of Ebon's Hall's mandate sent Highborn wayfarers and pilgrims to Anduz. Lita i Nadir i Riqueza's call for unity kept the passionate debates from turning into arguments. The firebrands proved to be driven chiefly by politics rather than Virtue or doctrine. Some likely bear auras of Freedom, but they do not seek to spread them. Their causes vary widely, and they blame the Senate and Military Council for sacrificing the Coast. Building the Burning Agora will restore them to prominence. Felix of the Far Tower's engineers offered to build the Anduz Pools bathhouse, creating a Freeborn sinecure, if it is commissioned in time.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: some firebrand hakima want the Military Council to concentrate its resources on wiping out the Druj.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: firebrands cite Grendel's years-long hold on Feroz as proof the Coast has been sacrificed by Imperial strategy.
n.Highguard: Highborn pilgrims and wayfarers, under Nim of Ebon's Hall's mandate, debated the firebrands at length but could not influence them. A Highborn chapterhouse, Felix of the Far Tower, has offered to build a bathhouse in Anduz.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: some firebrand hakima argue the western nations should be left to their own Vigilance against the Jotun.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn welcomed the Highborn, and the debates exposed the firebrands as passionate political idealists. Building the Burning Agora will restore them to prominence in Freeborn society, for better or worse.

t.Feroz: Mentioned in passing: firebrands point to Feroz languishing under Grendel control as a failure of Imperial strategy, and one Freeborn voice insists a firebrand would sooner have burned it than lost it.
t.Madruga: Mentioned in passing: firebrands cite Madruga, drowned in salt and exposed to Wreckers and Asaveans, as evidence the Coast has been sacrificed.
t.Reikos: Mentioned in passing: Reikos is home to the newly established Felix of the Far Tower chapterhouse, whose engineers propose the Anduz bathhouse and will return there if it is not commissioned in time.
t.Segura: The Highborn debates with the firebrands took place in Anduz, in Segura, where the Burning Agora is to be built. Highborn engineers offered to build the Anduz Pools there, a sinecure whose Keeper would receive 7 liao and 7 crowns each season.

The keys of blood.d: A Grendel Iontach raiding Wittal Grove sought to defect through the City of Locks. Janon, newly under enmity, sent heralds to curse Ossium and Sarangrave unless stopped. Sinokenon's mortal supporters came to Anvil fearing enmity. Arhallogen offered the Silver Chalice a way to poison a Grendel camp in Mareave for five hundred casualties. Surut offered generals aid, and Tharim's Ashen Knights camped in Karov. Agramant offered Navarri units an illegal venture to retake Therunin. Khobel Tavah set deadlines for Eilian Sweetwater's recovery and repeated its Everlasting Flame offer. Rhianos asked for Laroc to be ceded and charged the General of the Eastern Sky to stop a Druj sacrifice in Sarangrave. An Enterio quarry commission was also offered.

n.Dawn: Rhianos asked the Senate to cede Laroc's Tourney Grounds in return for 36 extra rings for Dawnish units questing or raiding from Astolat. Dame Aurum De Castellan, General of the Eastern Sky, was charged with recovering treasure from the Druj in Sarangrave.
n.Druj: Het Tavix Boneshaver's Druj were nearing the end of a vigil to sacrifice treasure to Agramant in Sarangrave. Surut was exacting ever greater tribute from the Druj and offering to help Imperial arson in Sanath, while Agramant-backed Navarri sought to retake Therunin from them.
n.Grendel: A Grendel mercenary company marched on Wittal Grove under Iontach Meddool Miniog, who secretly wished to defect. Arhallogen offered to poison a Golden Winds marine encampment in Mareave, causing five hundred casualties.
n.Highguard: Highguard's national assembly had urged its citizens, chapters and military units to aid refugees fleeing Therunin, so that Agramant would not be seen as their rescuer. Many of those refugees had fled to Reikos.
n.Imperial Orcs: Sinokenon was said to have favoured the Imperial Orcs since their nation's founding, approving of ordered legion life. Its heralds were particularly prevalent in the Unshackled's northernmost territory.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: a Grendel ship slipped past the Fjorknae fleets, and Azoth's orcish heralds were at first mistaken for Jotun emissaries.
n.Navarr: Agramant offered Navarri military units an illegal Reconquer Therunin venture alongside Dochas Weeping Glade, carrying a likely death sentence from the magistrates. The Navarr national assembly had urged its people to support the refugees instead.
n.The League: A herald of the City of Locks brokered the Grendel Iontach's defection, and Guise could accept him into the League if he is rescued. A commission was also offered to expand the Arratan Gamble in Tassato.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: Surut was indifferent to whether the Druj survive being crushed between the Empire and the Thule.
n.Urizen: Sinokenon's heralds were most numerous in Urizen, and Zenith's illuminates travelled to Anvil to lobby for it. Janon's heralds challenged Elagabala, Grandmaster of the Sevenfold Path, in Sarangrave, and Naris was named as the possible site of Khobel Tavah's Everlasting Flame.
n.Varushka: Janon's heralds challenged Vellenka Vanyanova to stop a curse on Ossium, and Tharim's Ashen Knights camped near Vorota in Karov. Surut praised General Aksel Reznov Razoradze, and Wieliczka's vales lobbied for Sinokenon.
n.Wintermark: Grendel mercenaries landed in Kallavesa to raid the Healing House of Wittal Grove. Theowold Vakarsson, Grimnir of Wittal Grove, was offered a contract to defeat them and escort the defecting Iontach to Anvil.

t.Astolat: Ceding the Tourney Grounds of Laroc to Rhianos would remove business investment in Astolat in favour of military units. Units questing or raiding from Astolat would gain an extra 36 rings.
t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: the wreckers' presence there makes naval superiority uncertain for Grendel mercenary companies.
t.Fjorknae: Mentioned in passing: a Grendel ship managed to evade the ships of the Fjorknae on its way to Kallavesa.
t.Forest of Ulnak: Mentioned in passing: Janon's heralds marched into Ossium across the border from the Forest of Ulnak.
t.Kallavesa: A Grendel mercenary ship sailed up the Gullet and landed near Wittal Grove, and its crew was marching on Wittal itself.
t.Karov: A legion of Tharim's Ashen Knights established a camp outside Vorota and intended to remain indefinitely, for reasons no one could learn.
t.Mareave: A Golden Winds marine encampment downstream of a Spring regio could be poisoned through Arhallogen's offer, costing the Grendel five hundred casualties.
t.Ossium: Janon's heralds threatened to curse Ossium with violent, unchecked passions unless the Shadowed Torchbearer stopped them. Soldiers of the Gryphon's Pride had failed to catch them.
t.Redoubt: The Empire may have chosen Rebekah's Leap in Redoubt for Khobel Tavah's Everlasting Flame, which would give the region a haunted quality and grim omens of coming doom.
t.Reikos: Mentioned in passing: many Navarri fleeing Therunin had taken refuge in Reikos.
t.Salt Flats of Sanath: Surut offered to help the Northern Eagle find further opportunities for arson the next time it infiltrates Sanath, if its general invokes his name.
t.Sarangrave: Janon's heralds threatened to curse Sarangrave unless Elagabala stopped them. Separately, the Druj were sacrificing treasure to Agramant here, and if they succeed Brokenhull's creatures would trouble its settlers.
t.Sea of Snow: Mentioned in passing: a Grendel ship avoided the monsters of the Sea of Snow on its way to Kallavesa.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: as the Unshackled's northernmost territory, it was one of the places where Sinokenon's heralds were particularly prevalent.
t.Tassato: The Architects of Iron and Stone proposed the Arratan Surety, a commission to boost the Arratan Gamble's white granite output.
t.Therunin: Agramant claimed to aid Navarri left in Therunin, backing Dochas Weeping Glade's survivor settlement. It offered an illegal venture to retake regions from the Druj.
t.Zenith: Illuminates of Zenith, long favoured by Sinokenon, travelled to Anvil to lobby against the Conclave declaring enmity on the eternal.

r.Kallavesa/Wittal Grove: Grendel mercenaries aimed to raid the Healing House of Wittal Grove. If the Iontach is not secured, the great work will provide no herbs until after the Autumn Equinox 388YE.
r.Karov/Wieliczka: Wieliczka's vales sometimes consult Sinokenon on rulership, and their representatives headed to Anvil to defend the relationship.
r.Ossium/Echofell: Janon's heralds kept returning to the Burned Glade in Echofell, where Vellenka Vanyanova was expected to confront them.
r.Redoubt/Naris: Rebekah's Leap in Naris may house the Everlasting Flame, and Khobel Tavah suggested pairing it with plans for the Lighthouse at Nikephoros.
r.Sarangrave/Kroll: Janon's heralds took the field around Slow Worm's Hill, calling out the Grandmaster of the Sevenfold Path to fight them.
r.Sarangrave/Turan Flats: The Druj held a vigil over treasure at the Stone of Thonkilch, and the General of the Eastern Sky was charged with recovering it. If they fail, Brokenhull's creatures would enter the region.
r.Tassato/Enterio: An outpost on the far side of the Arratan Gamble's largest vein was offered, adding five wains of white granite a season for three thrones more upkeep.
r.Zenith/Occursion: The illuminates of Occursion were described as long enjoying Sinokenon's favour.

The shadows fall behind you.d: The Ambition Assembly upheld a greater-majority call to consecrate Elos harbour, comparing General Umarth's sacrifice to Tian's. A General Assembly mandate to consecrate the site with true liao was proposed. If enacted, it would allow a Fist's Memorial sinecure with a Custodian drawn from Urizen or Wintermark. With a greater majority, it would also aid natural resupply for Urizen and Wintermark forces at Elos. Urizen would gift the Dissipating Silks schema to Runesmith's Law, and Kallavesi mystics would add Hero's Journey to Urizen Lore. Incommodus, then Mael of the Shattered Tower, offered a rival mandate that also celebrated Grendel Ambition, with unknown diplomatic effects. Eli of the Cenotaph's alternative would forgo the memorial and the exchanges.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: Wintermark's offer to share swamp-craft with Urizeni stargazers is meant to further Urizen's aims in the Druj-held Sarangrave.
n.Grendel: The Grendel were driven from Elos and their Maelstrom plot foiled. Rival mandates propose celebrating their audacious Ambition, though any effect on Grendel diplomacy or their view of Elos is unknown.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: cited as a barbarian nation that honours fallen enemies and reveres memorials to Imperial heroes.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: Apulian orcs were approached for comment on Grendel attitudes but declined to speculate, saying they now follow the Way.
n.Urizen: Urizen honours the Fist's sacrifice for Elos. If the consecration goes ahead, Urizen gains a possible memorial and custodian title, better resupply for its forces at Elos, and Hero's Journey in Urizen Lore, while Arethas's magicians would gift the Dissipating Silks schema to Wintermark.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark lost its oldest army, the Fist of the Mountains, whose sacrifice is to be honoured at Elos. A consecration could bring Wintermarkers the custodian title, better resupply for their forces there and Dissipating Silks in Runesmith's Law.

t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: Mael's mandate wording would make Elos a beacon of Ambition shining across the waters of Catazar to Attar.
t.Kallavesa: The Wintermark Assembly invited Urizeni stargazers to meet Kallavesi mystics, and the Crescent's Eye coven plans to add Hero's Journey to Urizen Lore if Elos is consecrated.
t.Redoubt: Elos's docks, retaken from the Grendel and back in service, are the proposed site of a true consecration of Ambition. This could draw pilgrims, a memorial and extra resupply for Urizen and Wintermark forces resting there.
t.Sarangrave: Mentioned in passing: Wintermark offered to share its swamp knowledge to help Urizen's aims in the Sarangrave.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: Apulian orcs, asked about Grendel attitudes, declined to comment as followers of the Way.
t.Zenith: Mentioned in passing: Zenith's great foundries helped Arethas's magicians copy the Dissipating Silks schema meant as a gift to Wintermark.

r.Redoubt/Naris: The proposed Fist's Memorial sinecure, producing liao for its Custodian, would be built in Naris, but only if Elos Harbour is consecrated with true liao.
r.Redoubt/Siluri: Mentioned in passing: Siluri's Academy of Arms is cited as a comparable place of pilgrimage.

The war makers.d: The Senate approved the army at the Spring Equinox 387YE on a motion by Rowyn of the Waystone Path, Senator for Hercynia, seconded by Tristan du Lac, Senator for Weirwater. The artisans of Dawn, the Marches, Varushka and the Imperial Orcs backed it, and Navarr gave more than eight hundred measures and ingots. Fifteen months later, after Cabal Lyktan's Hammers of Fury on Hercynia, the army was nearly ready. Rowyn weighed Siege, Resilient or Resourceful. Most Navarr wanted the lost Isaella's Dance left as a legacy, not reused as a name. The Star Forged was chosen. The ritual's lingering effects also briefly empowered Hercynian artisans and cambions.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: Dawn's artisans backed the motion to raise the army, and Weirwater's senator, Tristan du Lac, seconded it.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: the Imperial Orcs supported the motion through the backing of their artisans.
n.Navarr: Navarr gained its third army, the Star Forged, funded from across the nation and raised by the steadings' artisans. The nation now expects another army to follow, and its supply will fall by one if no further Navarr army is approved by the Summer Solstice 389YE.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: Varushka supported the motion through the backing of its artisans.

t.Hercynia: The new army was mustered in Hercynia around the forges of Treji. As the Hammers of Fury faded, the Chain shone brightly over the territory for a night, and Hercynian artisans and cambions gained brief potent benefits at the coming summit.
t.Weirwater: Mentioned in passing: Tristan du Lac, as Senator for Weirwater, seconded the motion to raise the army.

This is the end.d: The war between the cats and the birds in Apulian ended with the cats routed. Birdsong now drowns out the Black Plateau's malevolence for a season. Just under forty-five military units supported Sofonisba Amilcara and uncovered the Shadow Den of the Adumbral Volution beneath the Vicente School and Orphanage, a fane-like lair created by cultists. The lair was destroyed, but the empty orphanage vanished, apparently stolen by the Whisper Gallery. The duSesna Guild fled, and permanent night marks remain on the city. Sung rewarded the Map, who is now bound to the city. Sadogua and the Azoth proposed the Delectable Refectory and the Grand Laboratory, with unknown effects. The dramaturgical confluence largely ended, though its cause remains a mystery.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: thirteen Dawnish citizens, including members of House de Vere and the Amber Lance, are listed among those who supported the Map to the City Below.
n.The League: League businesses in Apulian are spared the Black Plateau's penalty for a season, and the League-appointed Sofonisba Amilcara is now bound to the city as Sung's Map to the City Below. The orphanage at the heart of the Whisper Gallery's lair has been lost, and the duSesna Guild has fled.
n.Urizen: Many Urizeni captains, including the Spiral Council's banner, aided the venture beneath Apulian. Every Urizeni magician who wishes it now keeps at least one of the clever, night-touched cats, which work hard and keep spires free of vermin.

t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: a Holberg professor of civil engineering dryly criticises the Azoth's unplanned approach to building the Grand Laboratory.
t.Spiral: A Night enchantment brought shared dreams of the war and renewed optimism across Spiral. The routed cats fled to the citadels and spires in the hills, and the heralds of Sadogua and the Azoth now call across the territory.

r.Spiral/Apulus: Songbirds now fill Apulian and shield it from the Black Plateau, and the Whisper Gallery's lair beneath the city has been destroyed, though its marks remain. Two proposed edifices for eternals could be built in Apulus until Summer 389YE.
r.Spiral/Cinion: Mentioned in passing: the Silver Flame's Fellowship of the Cinion Dawn appears among the banners supporting the Map to the City Below.

Thorn and bone.d: With its warding stones gone, the vallorn surged from Bendol into Nesustak Forest. Irra Harah's Wooden Fastness ward aided the defenders but also invigorated the vallornspawn, sharply raising casualties. When retreat was debated, the Black Thorns refused, and the Imperial forces pushed the spawn back; by the Summer Solstice the vallorn was quiescent. Meanwhile the Hidden Snake and Poison Crane, accompanied by Agramant-bound Winter husks and tortured souls, attacked from Lower Saarnath. They were routed, losing nearly twice the Empire's roughly five hundred dead, but they escaped pursuit, only to be cut down by Druj archers at the Sanath border. Both armies will disband after the Solstice. Axos completed its claim on Thornfen.

n.Druj: The Hidden Snake and Poison Crane were broken in Turan Flats and denied refuge by the Druj of the Salt Flats of Sanath. Both armies will disband, bringing an end to the Banded Snake and Marshlizard septs, and their Winter spirits and tortured souls threaten to be unleashed when they fall.
n.Highguard: The Granite Pillar defended the septs of the Mallum in Nesustak Forest and stood by the Black Thorns when retreat was considered. Rebels unable to fight fled west under Highguard's protection.
n.Navarr: The Black Thorns led the first line of defence against the vallorn and refused point blank to retreat, determined that Nesustak Forest should not share the fate of Eastring. Their resolve turned the tide.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: the trapping of the fleeing Druj is compared to the old Druj retreat from Holberg.
n.Urizen: The Citadel Guard held firm in the marsh to defeat the Druj invasion of Turan Flats, and studied the Winter magic binding the enemy armies. The Urizeni now face raids from Druj remnants, which will be far more dangerous if the two generals survive.
n.Varushka: The Boyar's Hasta fought between the Black Thorns and Granite Pillar against the vallorn, aided by Irra Harah's servants. The Golden Axe flanked and broke the Druj invaders in Turan Flats.

t.Brocéliande: Mentioned in passing: Kaela's Gift, which allows a painless death to Imperial citizens captured by the Druj or dying in vallorn miasma, extends into Brocéliande.
t.Hercynia: Mentioned in passing: Nesustak Forest is said to be left in no more danger from the vallorn than Northpines.
t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: the page recalls the Druj retreat from Holberg years ago as a precedent for the fleeing armies' fate.
t.Salt Flats of Sanath: Warriors of the Witness, the Spires of Rarckan and the Beacon of Iskrid lined the border and shot down the retreating Hidden Snake and Poison Crane, refusing to let the defeated armies return.
t.Sarangrave: The vallorn was driven back from Nesustak Forest and the Druj invasion of Turan Flats was defeated, though the trapped Druj armies remain in the territory. Axos completed its claim on Thornfen, and an Autumn enchantment helped reduce casualties across the territory.
t.Therunin: Mentioned in passing: the Tainted Basilisk's raising of Tharunind and the losses of East Ashes and Eastring are recalled, and Kaela's Gift extends into Therunin.

r.Hercynia/Northpines: Mentioned in passing: used as a comparison for the lingering vallorn danger now facing Nesustak Forest.
r.Salt Flats of Sanath/Lower Saarnath: Mentioned in passing: the Hidden Snake and Poison Crane launched their invasion across the border from Lower Saarnath into Turan Flats.
r.Sarangrave/Bendol: With its warding stones spent, the vallorn of Béantal Dol erupted outward before being driven back. It has now slipped into an uneasy quiescence, still uncontained and still very powerful.
r.Sarangrave/Bloodwater Marsh: Mentioned in passing: the vallorn had already been held back here by heroes using the Sentinel Gate, and the Bloodwater Spears joined the defence of Nesustak.
r.Sarangrave/Kroll: Thornfen's displaced population was exiled to Kroll. If the Winter spirits bound to the Druj armies are not contained, Agramant's ravenous husks will torment the region.
r.Sarangrave/Nesustak Forest: The vallorn surged across the river and nearly overwhelmed the forest before the Imperial armies and rebels drove it back and uprooted its seeds. The forest was spared lasting infestation, but heavy blood was shed where the Wooden Fastness empowered the spawn.
r.Sarangrave/Thornfen: Axos finished claiming Thornfen with the Senate's approval and exiled its population, save those with ties to the citadels. The region faces torment from Agramant's husks if the Druj Winter spirits are not trapped.
r.Sarangrave/Turan Flats: Imperial forces defeated the Druj invaders here, and the trapped remnants now face a final battle at the Fens of Varreth. If Het Trakaa's tortured souls are not exorcised, the region will be tormented.
r.Sarangrave/Whisperwood: The vallorn's eruption was weakened here, and Thornfen's exiles were sent here. Druj guerrillas with heralds of Surut also threaten to burn a weirwood tree at the Fingers of the Devourer.
r.Therunin/East Ashes: Mentioned in passing: the Pilgrim's Defiance's fight against Tharunind there is cited as a warning of what vallorn infestation brings.
r.Therunin/Eastring: Mentioned in passing: its loss to the Tainted Basilisk's malice spurred the Navarr's refusal to abandon Nesustak Forest.

Tomb of the Courageous.d: Ahraz's well-kept tomb in the Necropolis already draws hundreds of pilgrims, especially Freeborn and Imperial Orcs. One mandate would stress his part in freeing the orcs and let the Imperial Orcs support a fourth army or navy. The other would stress following one's own heart and let the Brass Coast support a fourth. If consecrated, a steward of the dead would come to Anvil at the Autumn Equinox to collect items of worth from Freeborn and orcs for the tomb, as the Highborn Assembly had requested. Firebrands and scriveners each want any statue in Kahraman to honour their side of Ahraz. Some still call him a heretic, and proof of this after consecration would cause a spiritual crisis.

n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: named as the foe the orcs are fighting in Mareave, whose spirits the orc-focused mandate would lift.
n.Highguard: Ahraz's tomb lies in the Highborn Necropolis, where experienced caretakers could handle more pilgrims, and the Highborn Assembly had backed unsealing it for items of worth. If consecrated, one of its stewards of the dead would come to Anvil to collect them.
n.Imperial Orcs: If the mandate honouring Ahraz's role in freeing the orcs passed, the Imperial Orcs could support a fourth army or navy. Their people were also invited to give items of worth to lie beside his orc honour guard.
n.The Brass Coast: If the mandate honouring Ahraz's devotion to his own convictions passed, Freeborn spirits would rise after years of hardship and the nation could support a fourth army or navy. Firebrands and scriveners were also vying over what a proposed statue to him should celebrate.

t.Feroz: Mentioned in passing: Governor Rahab's predations in Feroz are listed among the recent hardships of the Brass Coast.
t.Kahraman: The Senate or the Mistress of Monuments could commission a statue of Ahraz in Kahraman, where he spent his last years, honouring him as either a firebrand or a scrivener.
t.Madruga: Mentioned in passing: the depredations of the Dry Patricians in Madruga are cited among the Freeborn's recent sufferings.
t.Mareave: Mentioned in passing: the orc-focused mandate would bolster orcs fighting to keep their grip on Mareave against the Grendel.
t.Necropolis: Ahraz's tomb in the Necropolis would be the site of the consecration and draw even more pilgrims, which its caretakers could manage. A steward of the dead would gather items of worth to place there.

Tourney of two cities.d: Months of fierce but so far good-natured rivalry over recruits, including scores of duels, led the Barossa School and the Five Cities Military Academy to sponsor a tourney for young citizens who had recently passed their Test of Arms but were still young enough for the Sun Chamber. The first eight teams of three to register by 16:00 on Saturday would compete from 18:30. Each member took a different role (beater, bravo, cataphract, questing-knight or warcaster), which set their permitted weapons, under Iron Duke rules without consumables or barbarism. The sponsors lodged nine thrones with the Artisans Guild so each winner could buy a magic item worth up to three thrones. Runners-up each received a Skop's Mead or a Philtre of Heavenly Lore.

n.The League: Two League academies were using the tourney to find young citizens they could train as future officers for Imperial armies. They sponsored it with nine thrones.

t.Tassato: The city's two great military academies were locked in a rivalry over recruits. They channelled it into a jointly sponsored tourney at Anvil rather than more duels at home.

r.Tassato/Tassato Mestra: Home of the Five Cities Military Academy, one of the two sponsors competing to draw young recruits through the tourney.
r.Tassato/Tassato Regario: Home of the Barossa School of Imperial Strategy, the Five Cities Academy's rival and co-sponsor of the tourney.

Upgrade Palace of Apulian.d: Arising from the My friends are my estate Wind of Fortune, the project cost 80 wains of white granite and 30 thrones (240 crowns) in labour, and was due to take twelve months to build. Once complete, the upgrade would raise the fortification at Apulian to rank two and rename it the Palace of Mists. It would also make attacks on the region from the sea significantly harder, with seaborne assaults such as a shore offensive suffering a 20% penalty. Taxation from the territory would rise by five thrones a season. After the Summer Solstice, Casha di Apulian, Farren Silver Streams and Rhys Nighthaven each contributed a single crown towards the work.

n.The League: The League's defences in Spiral were set to be strengthened. Once the work was complete, the upgraded Palace of Mists would make its Apulian holdings harder to assault from the sea and bring in five more thrones a season in taxes.

t.Spiral: Work began on upgrading Spiral's Palace of Apulian. On completion it would make the territory harder to attack from the sea and raise its taxation by five thrones a season.

r.Spiral/Apulus: Apulus was the site of the Palace of Apulian, due to become the rank-two Palace of Mists after twelve months of building. Once finished, seaborne attacks on the region would suffer a 20% penalty.

Urizeni Experiment.d: The Stargazers salvaged warding stones from Bendol. Theodora and the Spear of the Seven were made responsible for casting Wardens of the Black Waste at two sites in Bloodwater Marsh, past ettercaps and vallornspawn. If both wards are made, Sorin will let the Empire summon a Basalt Citadel there. A third conjunction let the Warmage clear the way to the Turbulent Wellspring so the Archmage of Spring could perform Dance of Navarr and Thorn, at the risk of a pulse of chaotic energy. Agoska and Halyx delayed their visit to Anvil until Autumn, asking to bring a servant of Irra Harah and to be given Dreadful Ending. Servadi of the Severed Hornets offered the Sun Chamber a chance to explore the Hungry Earth.

n.Druj: The Druj legacy shapes the Sarangrave: the buruk tepel of the Thornwasp sept worked Severed Hornet labourers to death in the Hungry Earth mithril mines, and the Nesustak rebels hope to fell a Druj miasma pillar. Kaela's Gift lets captured Imperial citizens deny the Druj their corpses.
n.Navarr: The Archmage of Spring, Arwydd Clearbramble, was charged with performing Dance of Navarr and Thorn at the Turbulent Wellspring to join the Bendol vallorn heart to the trods. Doing so risks a chaotic pulse that could stir the hearts already connected.
n.Urizen: The Urizen National Assembly set the Stargazers to work on the vallorn. Theodora and the Spear of the Seven now carried the warding of Bloodwater Marsh, and Urizeni settlers stood to gain if the Druj miasma pillars were destroyed.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: the Boyar's Hasta is credited with helping save the Nesustak rebels, and the Hungry Earth mines are compared to the Crawling Depths in Ossium.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: the Sun Chamber last used the Door of Hidden Possibilities to scout in Sermersuaq, a year before this offer.

t.Brocéliande: Mentioned in passing: Kaela's Gift, which lets captured or miasma-stricken citizens choose a painless death, extends into Brocéliande.
t.Mountains of the Moon: Mentioned in passing: the entrance to the Hungry Earth caves lies on a plateau where the Sarangrave meets the Mountains of the Moon.
t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: the Thornwasp mithril operation is likened to the Crawling Depths in Ossium, and Ossium seconded a Senate statement on Nesustak Forest.
t.Sarangrave: The Sarangrave became the focus of efforts to contain the vallorn through new wards, a possible Basalt Citadel and a link to the trods. Its tangled rebel politics and the hidden mithril caves of the Hungry Earth were also coming to light.
t.Sermersuaq: Mentioned in passing: the Sun Chamber's Door of Hidden Possibilities was last directed to scout in Sermersuaq.
t.Therunin: Mentioned in passing: Kaela's Gift extends into Therunin.

r.Sarangrave/Bendol: The Stargazers salvaged surviving warding stones from Bendol. A conjunction to the Turbulent Wellspring offered the chance to connect its vallorn heart to the trods, which would also allow the proposed Eastern Citadel to be built.
r.Sarangrave/Bloodwater Marsh: Dilapidated warding stones at opposite ends of the marsh could be made permanent with Wardens of the Black Waste and a ring of ilium, if ettercaps and vallornspawn are driven off. If both wards are completed, a Basalt Citadel could be summoned here.
r.Sarangrave/Nesustak Forest: The Waterwalker and Bloodwater Spear rebels survived the vallorn but postponed their delegation until Autumn. They asked to bring a servant of Irra Harah to Anvil and to be given Dreadful Ending so they can destroy the forest's miasma pillar.
r.Sarangrave/Thornfen: Mentioned in passing: any Axou who have moved to Thornfen are presumed to suffer the same miasma-pillar effect as the Urizeni settlers.
r.Sarangrave/Whisperwood: Servadi of the Severed Hornets in Uklead revealed the Hungry Earth, a deadly narrow cave network in the southern cliffs once mined for mithril by the Thornwasp. A five-person conjunction offered the Sun Chamber a first look inside.

Viridian nemesis.d: Following Urizen last season, Navarr urged by Teleri Thornweaver (Greater Majority) and Leliel, Daughter of Armisael, turned to the League, which upheld its welcome 328-10. The cities offered five opportunities. Holberg engineers proposed the Boar's Hide, a costly level two fortification in Boar's Dell that would draw the vallorn's assault and boost Brocéliande's mana sites. Sarvos merchants proposed a Market of Everything ministry with a Merchant-Prince of the Vallornguard. Tassato proposed a Vallornguard Military Academy granting the Stem the Green Tide order. Temeschwari bishops suggested a mandate sending League military units against the vallorn. Spiral actors proposed plays about defeating the vallorn, with Apulian merchants offering five thrones through the Cat's Graces.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: fine wines from Dawn are cited among the goods traded in Sarvos's markets.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: Spiral's actors want the vallorn seen as an enemy that can be defeated once and for all, just like the Druj.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: a Sarvosi merchant prince scoffs that the Grendel think themselves masters of the Bay of Catazar though Dubhtraig's markets are barely twice Trivento's size.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: dramatising the recent triumph in Liathaven was suggested as a play subject but met little enthusiasm.
n.Navarr: The Navarr fulfilled their highest calling by sending their people, led by Teleri Thornweaver and Leliel, to arm and train the League, though steadings of Boar's Dell would bear the brunt of the vallorn's assault if Holberg's fortress were built.
n.The League: The League welcomed Navarr aid and each of its cities produced a proposal, from a fortress and a market ministry to a military academy, a Synod mandate for its bravos and inspiring plays, to prepare its people to join the Vallornguard.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: Sküld, in Thule-held Otkodov, is noted as a vallorn-infested territory lying north of Holberg.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: the Navarr worked with Urizen the previous season, and the League cities are said to be no less enthusiastic.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: rare metals from Varushka are listed among goods sold in Sarvos.

t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: Sarvos's trade reaches the Bay of Catazar at the docks of Cigno, and the Grendel are said to fancy themselves its masters.
t.Brocéliande: Holberg engineers proposed building the Boar's Hide fortress in Boar's Dell, which would draw the vallorn's attacks and raise investment in Brocéliande's mana sites while a vallornheart remains there.
t.Holberg: Holberg's engineers, after abandoning a scheme to channel the vallorn to their walls, proposed taking their skills to Brocéliande to build a grand fortification against it.
t.Liathaven: Mentioned in passing: the recent triumph in Liathaven was floated as a subject for an anti-vallorn play without much enthusiasm.
t.Otkodov: Mentioned in passing: its vallorn-infested region of Sküld is noted as lying north of Holberg.
t.Sarvos: Sarvosi merchants proposed a Market of Everything ministry to supply the Vallornguard with materials, herbs and mana crystals through a new Merchant-Prince of the Vallornguard.
t.Spiral: Spiral's actors and troupe magicians proposed using plays and dramaturgy to convince citizens the vallorn can be defeated, with a prize contest through the Cat's Graces.
t.Tassato: Amid the mustering of the League's third army, Tassatan bravos proposed an academy to train League soldiers in Vallornguard defensive tactics.
t.Temeschwar: Bishop Marko von Vardstein and the bravo Livinnia urged a Synod mandate so League military units could start fighting the vallorn immediately through relevant ventures.

r.Brocéliande/Black Boughs: Mentioned in passing: the Broch here is already fortified but deliberately built not to rouse the vallorn, as Black Boughs lies within the miasma.
r.Brocéliande/Boar's Dell: The proposed Boar's Hide would be raised on the foundations of Greenstead here, creating a level two fortification that would become the focus of the vallorn's assault on local steadings.
r.Brocéliande/Terunael: The vallorn of Terunael is the foe all these preparations target, and the Boar's Hide's mana benefit would last only until its vallornheart is destroyed.
r.Otkodov/Sküld: Mentioned in passing: Sküld is described as infested with the vallorn and lying north of Holberg.
r.Sarvos/Cigno: The Market of Everything ministry was proposed at Cigno, whose docks on the Bay of Catazar draw ships and trade from across the world.
r.Spiral/Apulus: Despite turmoil in its streets, Apulian merchants offered five thrones, to be awarded by the Cat's Graces at the Autumn Equinox, for the best play inspiring victory over the vallorn.
r.Tassato/Madeiras: The Vallornguard Military Academy was proposed for Madeiras, letting League armies with Vallornguard-appointed generals take the Stem the Green Tide order.

War games.d: Ambassador Thaumiel told Jarm that the perpetrators of the Lantir incursion were dead and that no Jarmish prince was responsible. Ambassador Cyrus told the Commonwealth that the Shuttered Lantern had traced it to deceased Commonwealth citizens and that Jarm and the world would be told. Jarm now demands everything the Empire knows, threatening war if the Empire is implicated. The Commonwealth demands secrecy, has put observers on the Conclave orders aiding it and has declared the Liberty Pact at an end. Cold Sun made only minor gains. The City of Locks offered a hidden smugglers' port on the Sea of Steel, and the Senate could make embassy letters public.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are not named; the only link is that the Autumn Archmage who arranged the summit is Vossk of Sarangrave Reforged.
n.Highguard: Both Highborn ambassadors, Thaumiel of Steeplechase Toll and Cyrus of Ebon's Hall, are at the heart of the crisis. Officers of the Pilgrim's Defiance, Seventh Wave and Valiant Pegasus visited the Commonwealth, which earned every Highborn general a heldenstein, gesetzstein and kriegsamulett, but further training opportunities are stalled until the crisis is resolved.

t.Sarangrave: Mentioned in passing: the territory appears only in the name of the Autumn Archmage, Vossk of Sarangrave Reforged, who urged Prospero to host the summit.

Warriors' Gate.d: Explorers mapped Warriors' Gate, a cold, flat tundra north of Suaq Fount. They found the frozen Lake of Sighs, Courtier's Wood, a carved trilithon dubbed the Gate of Winter and four pilgrim cairns. Armies cannot claim the region, but sites were found for Firebird Eorling's proposed Citadel of the Warm Hearth, which would anchor a claim. Two Blood-on-the-Snow regio, the Bloody Teeth and Treachers Dagger, were located, and a Wintermark mandate could turn the Hunt the Suaq Wastes venture against them. The Imperial Spymaster must choose to explore west, east or north next. Varushka and the Imperial Orcs pledged support, and the Whisper Gallery now offers a secret, criminal way to sabotage the effort.

n.Dawn: Dawnish adventurers pushed into Tsirku alongside the Winterfolk, and bold Dawnish captains may join the proposed hunt against Agramant's regio through the Hunt the Suaq Wastes venture.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the opening fiction refers to orc warriors from the arid plains of Mareave, Grendel's territory at the time, learning to ski.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orcs Assembly pledged to learn from Varushka and Wintermark by a vote of 60-0, so their captains can now Adventure in Tsirku. For now, however, the nation remains focused on its highest calling of exploring the ancestors of septs outside the Empire.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: no Jotun presence was found in Warriors' Gate, and the fallen thane Wemba the Bloody is said to have broken when the Jotun claimed his hall in Atalaq.
n.Navarr: A single Navarr band, Powell Open-Skies' Open Skies, joined the scouts, and its members likened the Gate of Winter to Hercynia's Gate of Summer.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: no Thule presence was found in Warriors' Gate, though the eastern route towards Urdur may bring explorers into contact with them.
n.Varushka: Varushka's Assembly backed Wintermark's exploration by 208 votes to 30, opening the Adventure in Tsirku venture to its champions. A proposed mandate would rally Varushkans to help explore and exploit the wastes while recognising Wintermark's claim to Tsirku.
n.Wintermark: Winterfolk led the exploration of Warriors' Gate and shared their cold-weather expertise with the rest of the Empire. They now face choices over building the Citadel of the Warm Hearth, mandating a hunt against Agramant's regio and advising the Spymaster on the next direction of exploration.

t.Hercynia: Mentioned in passing: the Gate of Winter reminded Navarr scouts of the Gate of Summer in Hercynia.
t.Kallavesa: Mentioned in passing: Varushkans call themselves cousins of the Suaq and Kallavesi.
t.Mareave: Mentioned in passing: the opening fiction describes orcs from the arid plains of Mareave learning to ski in Tsirku.
t.Otkodov: Mentioned in passing: magicians cite Otkodov as an example of dangerous lands being rich, and the eastern route may border Urdur.
t.Sea of Snow: Mentioned in passing: the western region of Tsirku may connect to the Sea of Snow, since great sea beasts must somehow reach the Grave of the Giants.
t.Sermersuaq: Sermersuaq is the gateway to Tsirku and suffers from monsters sent south from Agramant's regio. Destroying those regio would end the attacks, but the Smokehouse of Atalaq's provisions now go to explorers instead of boosting Sermersuaq's farms.
t.The Barrens: Mentioned in passing: the wealth of the wild Barrens is cited as proof that dangerous places tend to be rich.
t.Tromsa: Mentioned in passing: one possible route of exploration heads west towards Tromsa into barren, windswept country.
t.Tsirku: The first region of Tsirku, Warriors' Gate, has been mapped, revealing landmarks, rare plants and Blood-on-the-Snow regio. Three routes onward now await the Spymaster's choice, and exploration after the Autumn Equinox will be harder.

r.Otkodov/Urdur: Mentioned in passing: the ominous, rocky region east of Warriors' Gate may abut Urdur, making a Thule presence there more likely.
r.Sermersuaq/Suaq Fount: Mentioned in passing: Warriors' Gate lies directly north of Suaq Fount.
r.Sermersuaq/Suaq Wastes: The Hunt the Suaq Wastes venture, based at the Hall of Hunters, has fewer beasts left to hunt. A proposed mandate would turn it against the Bloody Teeth or Treachers Dagger, though success might eventually end the venture's purpose.
r.Sermersuaq/Tanikipari: Mentioned in passing: the bleeding rocks at the new regio resemble the Bleeding Ice found in Tanikipari by the Shuttered Lantern three years earlier.
r.Tsirku/Warriors' Gate: Explorers mapped the region's Lake of Sighs, Courtier's Wood, Gate of Winter and pilgrim cairns, and located two Blood-on-the-Snow regio. They also identified sites where the Citadel of the Warm Hearth could be built to claim the region for the Empire.

Who can you trust?.d: The scouting revealed that the Amber Scorpion sept, under the buruk tepel Taramid Skinwreath, was moving from Oerwealt into Ghul'thak Forest with its black lotus while Thule forces pursued it. A Sentinel Gate conjunction let Imperial heroes attempt to kill Skinwreath, carry the fragile plant home in its water-filled basin, seize sept treasures such as Black Wealt Wasps, and defeat Yaw'nagrah's heralds amid the Druj miasma. If the plant was recovered, the Military Council would choose between having an Imperial herbalist study it, which would kill it but yield one dose of powder, or entrusting it to the Karass rootwise. Two skirmishes were also offered: protecting Lenna Karass in Saltmarsh, and destroying a Thule-targeted day regio in Gloomsea.

n.Dawn: Many Dawnish nobles and banners joined the expedition to spy on the Thule, and a Druj warband slipped into the Dawnish-held Barrens to seize the Karass shaman Lenna Karass.
n.Druj: The Amber Scorpion sept was moving its black lotus, treasures and serfs under Taramid Skinwreath with the help of Yaw'nagrah's heralds, leaving it exposed to Imperial and Thule attack. A Druj raid also targeted Lenna Karass, apparently to punish the Karass for drawing close to the Empire.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: numerous Highborn citizens and banners are listed among those who spied on the Thule.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: several Navarr are listed among those who spied on the Thule, and Kaela's Gift is noted as extending into Therunin.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: a single League citizen is listed among those who spied on the Thule.
n.The Marches: Mentioned in passing: three Marcher citizens, including one of the Mournwold Sappers, are listed among those who spied on the Thule.
n.Thule: Thule forces were hunting Druj black lotus plants in Ulnak, and an Imperial seizure of Skinwreath's lotus would leave them furious and likely to demand reparations, though it would not breach the treaty. Their warlocks also sought to use a Gloomsea day regio to locate the Sawscaled Vipers' plant.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: three Urizen citizens are listed among those who spied on the Thule.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: many Varushkans are listed among those who spied on the Thule, and the Amber Scorpion sept is noted as having once dwelt in Ossium before Varushka claimed it.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: a sizeable group of Wintermark citizens, many from Stormspire, are listed among those who spied on the Thule.

t.Brocéliande: Mentioned in passing: Kaela's Gift, which lets Imperial citizens choose a painless death, is noted as extending into Brocéliande.
t.Forest of Ulnak: The forest was the scene of the contest for black lotus plants, with the Thule pursuing the Amber Scorpion sept and Imperial heroes offered the chance to strike at the Fetid Heart and at a day regio.
t.Mournwold: Mentioned in passing: the Mournwold Sappers banner appears in the list of those who spied on the Thule.
t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: the Amber Scorpion sept is said to have once dwelt in Ossium before the Varushkans claimed it.
t.Otkodov: Mentioned in passing: thwarting the Gloomsea warlocks would stop the Thule taking a black lotus back to Otkodov.
t.The Barrens: A small Druj raiding band crossed into the Barrens to capture Lenna Karass. Saving her would lead the Karass to replace true vervain in their tribute with cerulean mazzarine.
t.Therunin: Mentioned in passing: Kaela's Gift is noted as extending into Therunin.

r.Forest of Ulnak/Ghul'thak Forest: The Amber Scorpion sept moved into Ghul'thak Forest, and a Sentinel Gate conjunction to the Fetid Heart there offered the chance to kill Taramid Skinwreath and seize his black lotus under a Druj miasma.
r.Forest of Ulnak/Gloomsea: Thule-allied warlocks were heading for the Islet of Calm, a powerful day regio in Gloomsea, and Imperial magicians were offered a skirmish to destroy it with Wind of Mundane Silence and hide the evidence.
r.Forest of Ulnak/Oerwealt: Mentioned in passing: the Amber Scorpion sept's forces are reported to have moved out of Oerwealt into Ghul'thak Forest.
r.The Barrens/Saltmarsh: A Druj warband slipped into Saltmarsh to capture the young Karass shaman Lenna Karass, and the Envoy to the Karass was charged with intercepting it.
